raw.description:
About Decagon

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.

Our technology enables industry-defining enterprises like Avis Budget Group, Block’s Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.

We’re building a future where customer experiences are being redefined from support tickets and hold music to faster resolutions, richer conversations, and deeper relationships. We’re proud to be backed by world-class investors who share that vision, including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, and Index Ventures, along with many others.

We’re an in-office company, driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity. Our values — Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner’s Mindset, and The Polymath Principle — shape how we work and grow as a team.

About the Role

Decagon is seeking a Solutions Architect – Voice, a technical hire who will define how enterprises deploy Decagon's AI agents into live voice and contact center environments. This role sits at the intersection of pre-sales engineering, telephony architecture, and enterprise contact center strategy. You will act as a trusted advisor to enterprise prospects and customers, guiding them through complex, ambiguous voice deployment conversations—from SIP trunking and call routing to media handling and real-time transcription—ensuring Decagon integrates seamlessly into their existing contact center platforms while meeting latency, reliability, and compliance requirements.

As an early hire in this function, you will define best practices for voice deployment solutioning, partner cross-functionally with Sales, Product, and Engineering, and set the standard for how Decagon engages with enterprises running mission-critical contact center operations. You will establish technical credibility with stakeholders across the C-suite, telephony and network teams, contact center operations, and CX leadership.

In this role, you will

  • Partner with Account Executives to discover, qualify, and design voice deployment solutions that address customer telephony constraints and deliver measurable containment and CX outcomes.

  • Navigate ambiguous conversations about a customer's contact center landscape, translating diverse environments (Genesys Cloud CX & Engage, Amazon Connect, Cisco UCCE/CVP, Google CCAI) into clear integration and deployment strategies for Decagon's voice platform.

  • Design SIP integration approaches—BYOC trunking, REFER-based transfer, header propagation, and media/streaming paths (Websockets, Audio Connector, External Voice Transfer)—tailored to each customer's topology and security posture.

  • Diagnose complex, multi-leg call flows down to the packet level, and establish repeatable methods for tracing and resolving SIP and media issues in production.

  • Establish scalable pre-sales processes, deployment playbooks, and reusable reference architectures to support growth.

Your background looks something like this

  • 8–10+ years in customer-facing technical roles (Solutions Architect, Solutions Engineer, Technical Account Manager, Product Manager) with a focus on voice, telephony, or contact center platforms.

  • Deep fluency in enterprise contact center platforms—Genesys, Amazon Connect, Cisco, or Google CCAI—and the SIP/telephony fundamentals underneath them (trunking, transfer semantics, codecs, SRTP, DTMF).

  • Hands-on experience with CPaaS infrastructure such as Twilio or Telnyx, including BYOC configuration and programmable voice.

  • Demonstrated success navigating ambiguous technical conversations with enterprise customers, asking the right discovery questions, and collaborating through uncertainty.

  • Strong ability to engage diverse stakeholders—from network engineers to CX and contact center leaders—and translate voice requirements into actionable deployment strategies.

Even better if you have

  • 2+ years selling or architecting AI/ML or conversational voice solutions in enterprise environments.

  • Experience in a high-growth startup where you built pre-sales practices from the ground up.

  • Hands-on packet-level SIP diagnostics experience (pcap analysis, Wireshark/Scapy) and comfort reading raw signaling.

  • Familiarity with real-time speech stacks (STT/TTS), call recording and compliance patterns (SIPREC), and multi-leg call correlation.

Benefits

We proudly offer the following benefits for our full-time employees:

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits for you and your family

  • Life Insurance and Disability Benefits

  • Retirement Plan (e.g., 401K, pension)

  • Parental Leave

  • Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

  • Monthly stipend to support your wellness, lifestyle, and work-life balance

  • Daily lunches and snacks in the office to keep you at your best

  • Take what you need vacation policy (subject to local requirements; UK employees receive 25 days of statutory leave)

These benefits are described in more detail in Decagon’s policies, may vary by location, and can change at any time according to applicable compensation and benefits plans.

raw.title: Site Associate - Editions Bermondsey
raw.description:
Title: Site Associate (Part time)

Location: Bermondsey
Pay: £14.40 per hour

Hours: 20

 

About Deliveroo Editions

With a dash of hard-work, a sprinkle of teamwork and a whole dollop of creativity, we created “Editions” which is our ‘dark kitchens’ business. We have partnered with some fantastic restaurants such as Wagamama, Starbucks, Pho and Gourmet Burger Company to help further connect them with hungry customers.

Delivery-only kitchens have never been higher profile, or more valuable for improving service and selection for customers. Deliveroo Editions were the world's first delivery-only kitchens, and we are still the market leaders in helping our restaurant partners succeed. What’s even more exciting is that we’re expanding our portfolio further.

Great people help to drive our business forward and we are always looking for more to join our sites. If you don’t have the exact experience, that’s okay, we’d still love to hear from you.

Does this sound tasty to you? Take a look at our Site Associate role and apply below to join the Roo family.

About the role

The Site Associate role covers a wide range of tasks across the Editions site. You will ensure that the site is clean, support the wider operation of the site to ensure that our loyal customers receive their orders as quickly as possible from our trusted partners.

Responsibilities will include:

  • You will report into the Site Manager and the site management team.

  • Ensuring that the cleanliness of the site is maintained to a high standard by cleaning as you go throughout the shift as well as regular deep cleaning of various equipment throughout the week

  • Cleaning communal areas, such as staff room, bathrooms, stock rooms, maintaining site health and safety standards at all times

  • Working with the management team to ensure a safe and clean site by participating in regularly checking

  • Assisting with dispatching, which will include running food from our partners to the dispatch area, assisting with orders and communicating with our riders

  • Supporting our partners by keeping kitchen equipment clean and ready for use throughout the shift with the pot wash

Who we are looking for

  • You radiate positivity!

  • You have a great attitude to work, you are driven and have willingness to learn

  • You are a team player, punctuality and reliability is your forte

  • You always go above and beyond, you’re looking to progress in your career

  • You can work autonomously but you LOVE working with a fantastic team and with our partners

  • You like to solve problems, making recommendations on how to improve daily tasks

  • Previous experience in a Kitchen Porter or Kitchen Cleaner role is a bonus, but don’t worry if you haven’t, if you have the right attitude and drive, we can train you.

What to expect from the interview process

  • Step 1: apply for any role you'd like to be considered for - we'd love to hear from you!

  • Step 2: if your application is successful, one of our recruitment team will be in touch to say hello and understand more about your experience

  • Step 3: if we decide to progress your application, you will be invited to an onsite interview with one of the site managers

  • Step 4: We'll come back to you quickly after your interview to let you know the outcome!

Benefits

  • 25 days holiday, increases with length of service

  • Free food and LOTS of it

  • Access to Deliveroo Plus (no delivery fee on all orders)

  • Life assurance

  • Access to discounts in other companies via our benefits portal

  • Employee assistance programme

  • Company paid team meals and nights out

  • Online learning courses delivered by global universities

  • Clear career development path

Why Deliveroo


Our mission is to transform the way you shop and eat, bringing the neighbourhood to your door by connecting consumers, restaurants, shops and riders. . We are transforming the way the world eats and shops by making access to food and products more convenient and enjoyable. We give people the opportunity to buy what they want, as they want it, when and where they want it.
We are a technology-driven company at the forefront of the most rapidly expanding industry in the world. We are still a small team, making a very large impact, looking to answer some of the most interesting questions out there. We move fast, value autonomy and ownership, and we are always looking for new ideas.

Workplace and Diversity

At Deliveroo we know that people are the heart of the business and we prioritise their welfare. We offer multiple great benefits in areas including health, family, finance, community, convenience, growth and relocation.

We believe a great workplace is one that represents the world we live in and how beautifully diverse it can be. That means we have no judgement when it comes to any one of the things that make you who you are - your gender, race, sexuality, religion or a secret aversion to coriander. All you need is a passion for (most) food and a desire to be part of one of the fastest growing startups in an exciting space.

raw.title: Head of Technical Support
raw.description:
📍 London (Hybrid — 2 days onsite)

🕒 Permanent | Start ASAP

 

We’re Making Travel Effortless. Join Us.

Travel is essential, whether it’s visiting family, starting a new adventure, or taking a career defining trip. Yet today, over 4 billion airline passengers rely on tech that hasn't changed in decades.

At Duffel, we’re rebuilding the infrastructure underpinning the global travel industry. Backed by top-tier investors (Benchmark, Blossom, Index Ventures, and Kima Ventures) and born out of Y Combinator (S18), we’re simplifying complex systems to build the future of travel

About the role

As Head of Technical Support, you’ll lead our team of Technical Support Engineers and take responsibility for the quality, effectiveness and development of the function.

You’ll build a team that combines strong technical investigation with clear, thoughtful customer communication. You’ll coach engineers, establish effective ways of working and ensure customers receive dependable support as their integrations grow in complexity and scale.

You’ll stay close to the work: reviewing investigations, helping with significant escalations and understanding where our products or processes create friction. Your impact will come from strengthening the whole team’s ability to resolve problems and turning what we learn from support into lasting improvements.

You’ll work closely with Engineering, Product, Partner Engineering, Partner Management and Travel Operations. Technical Support owns day-to-day API questions, troubleshooting and the customer support response to technical incidents. Partner Engineers own strategic technical relationships and solution architecture; Implementation Managers own implementation programmes.

What you’ll do

  • Lead and develop the team. Set clear expectations, provide regular coaching and feedback, support career development and address performance issues constructively. Hire and onboard engineers as the team grows.

  • Own support quality. Establish standards for technical investigation, written communication, case ownership and follow-through. Ensure customers understand what is happening, what comes next and who is responsible.

  • Build a dependable support operation. Improve triage, prioritisation, queue management, handovers and escalation paths. Plan staffing and coverage around customer needs and agreed service commitments, with a sustainable workload for the team.

  • Strengthen technical capability. Help engineers investigate API behaviour, interpret logs and request traces, reproduce integration issues and distinguish customer configuration problems from platform or supplier issues.

  • Lead significant customer escalations. Coordinate the support response, establish customer impact and keep communication clear through to resolution. Work with Engineering on diagnosis and recovery, involving Partner Engineering where an issue creates a wider strategic risk.

  • Make collaboration effective. Give Engineering actionable escalation reports with evidence, reproduction steps and impact. Work with Travel Operations on booking and supplier issues, and with implementation teams to ensure new integrations enter support with the context the team needs.

  • Improve the product through support. Identify recurring problems and turn them into clear recommendations for Product and Engineering. Track whether fixes, documentation and product changes actually reduce customer friction.

  • Make support easier to deliver. Develop troubleshooting guides, internal knowledge, customer documentation and useful tooling. Apply automation and AI where they improve accuracy, speed and access to help.

  • Use evidence to guide decisions. Monitor response and resolution performance, ageing work, reopened cases, customer feedback and team capacity. Use that information to prioritise improvements and make clear recommendations about investment.

What we’re looking for

  • Experience managing and developing a technical support or support engineering team serving business customers.

  • A track record of improving both customer outcomes and how a support function operates.

  • Strong technical understanding of APIs, HTTP, authentication, webhooks and integrations, with enough practical depth to guide investigations and earn the trust of engineers.

  • Comfort working with logs, SQL and scripts to investigate problems or improve support workflows.

  • Experience handling consequential customer escalations, including situations where the cause or resolution is initially uncertain.

  • Ability to explain technical issues to developers, business stakeholders and senior leaders.

  • Sound judgement about urgency, customer impact and competing priorities.

  • Evidence of effective hiring, coaching, performance management and delegation.

  • The ability to influence Product, Engineering and commercial teams through clear reasoning and useful evidence.

  • Comfort building and improving a function in a growing company, while remaining involved in its day-to-day work.

Experience that would be useful

  • Supporting an API platform, developer product or infrastructure business.

  • Working with enterprise customers running important production integrations.

  • Leading support across different time zones.

  • Improving support tooling, knowledge management, self-service or automation.

  • Experience in travel technology, payments or another industry with complex external dependencies.

You don’t need to have worked in travel or held this exact title. We’re interested in the teams you’ve developed, the problems you’ve solved and the judgement you bring.

What success looks like

During your first six months:

  • Engineers have clear expectations, regular coaching and practical development plans.

  • Customer issues have clear ownership, appropriate prioritisation and dependable communication.

  • You have established a trustworthy baseline for support performance and delivered measurable improvements in the most important areas.

  • Escalations reach the right teams with better evidence and fewer unnecessary handovers.

  • Recurring problems are being addressed through product changes, documentation or tooling.

  • Duffel has a clear plan for the support capacity and capabilities needed as the business grows.

Why You’ll Love Working at Duffel

We believe in true ownership. That’s why every permanent employee gets equity in the business.

Perks That Actually Matter:

✈️ Travel Allowance: We literally pay you to get out of town and explore the world.

🏝️ Work From Anywhere: Flexibility is built in. Work remotely, or take advantage of our Sabbatical Policy.

⚡ Electric Car Scheme: Roll up in a brand-new EV with eco-friendly tax savings.

⚖️ Work-Life Harmony: Flexible bank holidays, generous family leave, and a dedicated volunteering day.

📚 Growth Tools: Paid study days to level up your skills, plus a solid pension and cycle-to-work scheme.

🏥 Health & Wellbeing: Private healthcare, eye test cover, and season ticket loans.

🏡 Family Leave (maternity, paternity and adoption): Big support for life’s biggest moments, 26 weeks fully paid.

The Details

📍 Location: Shoreditch, London (Hybrid: In-office Tuesdays & Thursdays).

🧠 Interview Process: Simple & transparent: (change accordingly to role)

  1. Recruiter Screen

  2. Hiring Manager Chat

  3. Technical Case Study

  4. Final Stage Interview.

We are an equal opportunities employer. We believe that the key to our success is employing a diverse team, that's why recruitment decisions are only based on your experience and skills. We value your ability to problem solve and build amazing things so we welcome applications for everyone - regardless of age, sex, disability, sexual orientation, race, religion or belief.

Note to recruitment agencies Duffel does not accept speculative CV's from external parties. Any unsolicited CV's sent to us will be treated as property of Duffel, and any attached terms and conditions associated with these CV's will be null and void.

raw.title: Credit Strategy Analyst
raw.description:
We’re on a mission to back the UK’s small businesses like no one else 🚀

Small businesses are the backbone of the economy, and we’re here to help them win. We’ve built a platform that uses clever data to get them the funding they need in minutes, not weeks.

At Funding Circle, we have the restless energy of a fintech start-up with the stability of a public company. It’s a unique mix that gives Circlers the autonomy to take ownership and the scale to make an impact that truly counts.

We’re a high-performing team that chooses to lift each other up. We challenge, we champion, and we have each other’s backs - because we know that when we stand together, we move faster and build better.

The impact is real: Last year alone, the businesses on our platform generated £7.2bn for the UK economy 📈 Come and join a mission that matters!

[Read our Impact Report] | [See our Trustpilot]

The role ⚡

📍 London (Hybrid) | 🤝 3 days in the office | 💰 Competitive Salary + Benefits

This role sits in the Credit Risk team who are hugely influential to our overall lending process. They look at measuring our risk, optimising our credit risk funnel and forecasting the performance of our loan portfolios. To do this, they work with the credit risk modelling, engineering, data management, capital markets and business operations teams to truly understand our objectives and shape analytical solutions.

Focusing on our Credit Risk lending capabilities, you’ll be given the opportunity to think outside the box and come up with a wide range of suggestions and ideas to optimise our ability to lend to small businesses, while also delivering strong returns for our investors.

  • Primarily responsible for monitoring our Credit Strategy to identify useful trends and opportunities to optimise our lending strategy

  • Involved with all aspects of credit strategy analytics, from loss rate forecasting to segmentation analysis

  • Guiding business decisions by carrying out ad hoc analysis, providing credit risk insights and recommendations for optimising credit risk strategies and business processes

  • Collaborate with experts from different functions, particularly Engineering and Operations, to ensure daily running of our lending business and to implement any Credit Strategy changes

What we’re looking for 🌱

  • A degree in a highly numerical discipline (e.g., Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Computer Science, or Physical Sciences)

  • Open to entry-level candidates and recent graduates. Prior internship or work experience in credit risk, portfolio analytics, or banking is a strong plus, but not required.

  • Ability to guide decisions through data—from defining the underlying business question to analyzing datasets and communicating actionable recommendations.

  • Excellent communication skills, particularly with regards to translating data analyses and numbers into actionable insights tailored to the audience

  • Intermediate-to-advanced Excel skills.

  • Practical coding proficiency in at least one analytical language (SQL, Python, or R). Candidates with SAS experience or demonstrated aptitude to learn new languages quickly are also considered.

  • Curious and eager to learn, and comfortable working independently on solving open-ended problems.

  • Able to take ownership of redesigning departmental workflows, using AI to automate complex tasks and drive operational efficiency

  • Competently able to Identify high-impact AI use cases and implement advanced prompting techniques to solve multi-layered business challenges

  • Prior exposure to credit risk analytics or banking (retail, corporate, or investment) is advantageous but not required.

We’re building a place where everyone truly feels they belong. Even if your past experience doesn't align perfectly with every requirement, we'd still love to hear from you.

Why join us? 💜

We back you to build an incredible career and by joining us, you'll be part of one of The Sunday Times Best Companies to Work For 2026! As a flexible-first employer, we use a "best of both" approach. We’ll see you in our London office to collaborate – with barista coffee and subsidised Just Eat lunches on us!

Our Circler Proposition focuses on five areas:

  • Flexibility: We provide a benefit allowance you can tailor to your own life and family.

  • Health: This includes private medical and dental, health assessments, and access to a digital GP.

  • Wealth: We offer life assurance, share schemes, and financial coaching.

  • Development: You get a dedicated annual learning allowance to help you level up.

  • Lifestyle: We have electric car and cycle-to-work schemes, plus season ticket loans.

We also have award-winning parental leave policies. We're here to support you through the big life moments, from fertility treatments to new additions to the family.

Ready to join a mission that matters? We’d love to chat!

You’ll make a real difference for our customers and your team from day one. We believe the fastest way to grow is by doing, so we give you the ownership to run with things and see real-time results.

We are looking for a Data Platform Engineering Manager to join our Data Platform Engineering team which sits under Tech and Data. We’re partway through a migration to a modern Snowflake-based platform, so you’ll join at a pivotal point where your decisions will shape how we work for years to come

Reporting directly to the Head of Data Engineering, You’ll partner closely with our Technical Lead and Principal Engineer: while they drive architecture and technical patterns, you will own the delivery engine, team health, career progression, and stakeholder alignment that turns strategy into reality.

  • Lead, manage, and mentor a team of data platform engineers, fostering a collaborative, innovative, and inclusive team culture.

  • Champion a product mindset for internal tooling, ensuring our platform empowers domain teams to build quickly and safely without bottlenecks

  • Oversee the recruitment, onboarding, and performance management processes for the team. Set clear goals and expectations, providing regular feedback and guidance to team members.

  • Oversee the planning, execution, and delivery of projects within the data platform roadmap, ensuring timely and high-quality outcomes.

  • Manage the team's backlog, prioritise tasks effectively. Define and track key performance indicators (KPIs) for platform health and team delivery.

  • Build strong relationships and collaborate effectively with key stakeholders, including technical and business leaders. Understand stakeholder needs and translate them into actionable requirements for the data platform.

  • Communicate the team's roadmap, progress, challenges, and successes clearly and proactively to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Actively invest in the career development of your team members through coaching, mentoring, and identifying growth opportunities. Create personalised development plans and support engineers in acquiring new skills and expertise. Foster a culture of continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and technical curiosity within the team.

 

What we’re looking for 🌱

We value deep expertise, but a growth mindset and good energy are what really make our team click. We’re a group that chooses to lift each other up and think smart every day.

  • Solid understanding of modern data platform architectures (,e.g. Snowflake, data mesh/lakehouse, dbt, Airflow, streaming vs. batch pipelines, data contracts)

  • Proven experience managing and leading high-performing data engineering teams in a product-driven environment

  • Proven track record of mentoring and developing engineers, fostering a culture of technical excellence, innovation, and professional growth.

  • Demonstrable experience in managing project delivery, including planning, prioritisation, and execution.

  • Experience with Agile/Scrum methodologies.

raw.description:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We are looking for a highly skilled solicitor to lead our EMEA Commercial legal team. Reporting to the Deputy General Counsel, you will primarily interface with our Go-To-Market team to help ensure the fast, efficient execution of our agreements with customers, and you will also have exposure to product, privacy and competition issues.

What You'll Do

Generative AI has the power to greatly change the world and directly impact how things get done. Harvey is at the forefront of this change, and our mission is to make generative AI actionable and useful for our customers. This is a fast moving environment (we are a start-up!) that is serving some of the world’s most renowned law firms and professional organizations. And this role will put you in the center of all of this.

More specifically, you will:

  • Lead the international multi-office Commercial legal function in the UK and EU, continuing to build a strong substantive, organizational and relationship foundation for the legal presence in the region

  • Mentor and lead a high-functioning team (including managers) in the drafting, review, and negotiation Commercial AI SaaS contracts

  • Hire others in the region as we expand


What You Have

  • UK or Dublin-based solicitor with 12+ years experience, both with the commercial or technology division of a leading private practice law firm, and subsequently in-house with a technology company supporting SaaS or technology Go-To-Market or Business Development teams

  • Experience building and managing high-functioning teams

  • Transactional background, including with technology and/or IP licensing commercial agreements

  • Experience with government sales is a plus, as is working internationally with US-based leadership

  • Ability to think creatively, function independently and work proactively in a fast-paced environment

  • Team-focused and collaborative work style; willingness to build expertise and solve new challenges in an evolving practice

  • Hyper-responsive and service-oriented attitude

  • Bonus qualifications include experience with AI, and a love for solving hard problems with a small tight-knit team

AI Developer for Learning Products
raw.description:
Jellyfish is a full service global digital agency, combining strategy, creative, data and media buying and planning expertise with technology under one integrated roof. With almost 2,000 Jellies across 38 offices worldwide, we are the unconventional global marketing partner of the future.

We understand both brand and activation. We ensure our clients reach, influence and connect with the right audiences and fans based on data that reveals the insights to deliver exceptional creative solutions across any platform. In short, we create and deliver culturally relevant creativity that cuts through the clutter and sets hearts (and feeds) on fire.

As part of the Brandtech Group we’re at the forefront of the deployment of GenAI tools across every aspect of what we do and in PencilPro we have the world’s No 1 generative AI platform, revolutionising the process of creative production, distribution and performance prediction.

Job Description

Reporting to the Head of People Development, you will turn our learning ideas into working products. Our Education and Experience team designs how more than 7,000 people across the Brandtech Group learn, grow and perform, and we prototype fast with AI coding tools. You'll take those prototypes and make them into reliable, secure apps that people use every day.

Our goal is to turn all of our learning into an agentic solution that meets employees where they are, so they can learn in real time, in the flow of work. You'll join a small, distributed team, work alongside a senior architect who owns our core platform, and grow your craft as our products grow.

Responsibilities

  • Build and Ship Learning Products

    • Turn learning and performance designs into working software and app features.

    • Help take AI-built prototypes into production, from the front end through to the database.

    • Build wireframes and working prototypes to test new ideas quickly with real users.

    • Fix bugs, ship improvements and keep our products running smoothly.

  • Build Agentic Learning Experiences

    • Build learning experiences that live inside the tools people already use, with no separate login.

    • Build on the core platform and agent architecture owned by our senior architect, so employees get the right support at the moment they need it.

  • Connect Systems and Data

    • Work with the People Systems team to connect our learning products with our HR system, skills platform and role frameworks.

    • Maintain integrations across the learning technology stack.

    • Support the move from several learning platforms to one, including migration of content and records.

  • Work as Part of a Distributed Team

    • Collaborate with instructional designers and learning partners across time zones.

    • Put the employee first, testing with real users and gathering feedback to improve.

    • Document what you build so others can use, support and extend it.

Qualifications

  • About 1–3 years building web applications, internal tools or digital products (professional, freelance or substantial personal projects).

  • Hands-on experience with Python and FastAPI, or a similar Python web framework.

  • Experience with PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy and Alembic, or an equivalent ORM and migration workflow.

  • You have built server-rendered pages with Jinja2 or a similar templating engine.

  • Proficient building with Claude Code.

  • You have deployed at least one working app (personal, academic or professional). Please, share it with us through a portfolio, GitHub or a live demo.

  • You generate unique ideas and experiment with new methods and technologies to solve complex issues.

  • When faced with a problem, you collaborate with the appropriate people to evaluate different options and find practical solutions.

  • You embrace challenges as opportunities and seek feedback to enhance your skills.

Note: We emphasise skills, expertise and behavioural attributes over years of experience and traditional degrees. If you want to join our collaborative team, we invite you to apply today with your resume in English.

Additional Information

Join Jellyfish and experience a workplace where we prioritise your growth, celebrate your contributions, and empower you to tailor your work environment to suit your needs.

💫 Custom Work Environment: Work remotely for up to 60% of your days and shape your day between 8am. and 6:30pm with flexible working hours.

👪 Family Support: Enjoy 14 weeks of paid leave for primary caregivers and 4 weeks of paid leave for secondary caregivers. We also provide £1000 (or equivalent) towards courses for returning primary caregivers to support your transition back into work.

Unfortunately, there has been an increase in fake recruiters impersonating Jellyfish and unlawfully using our brand name. If you are unsure if an email with a job offer you have received is genuinely from Jellyfish, or if you suspect any fraudulent activity, please report it to Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

raw.title: Global Programmatic Architect
raw.description:
At Jellyfish, we believe in the power of diverse perspectives and inclusive collaboration. We welcome individuals who excel in collaborative, varied teams and value the unique contributions that each person brings to the table.

Jellyfish is a global digital marketing agency; a unique fusion of tech enthusiasts, creative minds, and media and data experts all united to empower our clients along their digital journey. Our commitment to embracing diverse perspectives fuels our innovation and strategies that challenge the status quo, reinvent media activation, and craft influential stories for our global clients and their customers. Join us in shaping a future where business growth and personal fulfilment go hand in hand.

Job Description

The Global Programmatic Lead (Programmatic Architect) is the senior technical practice leader for Programmatic Media across Jellyfish, sitting within the Domain Specialists hub and reporting to the Chief Solutions Officer - Media, Strategy & AI (CSO). You are the global custodian of how Jellyfish architects, engineers, automates, and commercialises programmatic activation across DSPs, SSPs, curation layers, bidding algorithms, and data clean rooms.

This is a senior role, there is no direct line management or people management but you are expected to collaborate with activation team leads & regional media leadership to affect positive change for Jellyfish clients. You are not running campaign ops or managing direct reports; you are the agency’s most senior programmatic technologist and systems architect. You define the global practice, codify frameworks for scaled delivery, contribute to our proprietary product roadmap, lead high-stakes pitches to win new business, drive technical advancement through strategic ad-tech partnerships, and serve as principal technical counsel to our highest-value global enterprise clients.

You partner closely with regional media and delivery leads across NA, EMEA, and APAC. While regional delivery teams execute programmatic campaigns in their local markets, you set the technical architecture, bidding methodologies, automation workflows, and delivery standards they operate from.

 

50% Product, Commercial & Technical Partnerships · 50% Client Strategic & Technical Leadership

The role is an intentional 50/50 split:

  • 50% Practice & Product Architecture: Designing buying & audience strategies, automation hooks/MCP integration, steering ad-tech integration roadmaps, managing top-tier tech partnerships (Google, The Trade Desk, Amazon, etc.), and spearheading major pitches.

  • 50% Client Strategic Leadership: Serving as principal programmatic strategist and trusted technical advisor for Tier-1 accounts, driving technical maturity (signal resilience, clean rooms, custom algorithms) and unlocking incremental retained revenue.

     

Your primary responsibilities will include:

 

1. Product Strategy, Automation & Technical Partnerships (50%)

  • Define the Global Programmatic Methodology: Own and update the global programmatic playbook, codifying standards across audience intelligence, bidding, algorithmic optimisation, curated marketplaces (PMPs/PG), dynamic creative optimisation (DCO), and identity/signal resilience.

  • Codify Delivery & Drive Automation: triage execution into fully automated, hybrid, or human-assisted workflows, handing off artefacts to delivery and MSP teams to streamline campaign build times and eliminate operational friction.

  • Contribute to Proprietary Product Evolution: Partner directly with Jellyfish Product teams to feed technical requirements, data schemas, and API automation hooks into internal tooling.

  • Ad-Tech Partnerships & Frontier Innovation: Own strategic technical relationships with core platforms (DV360, The Trade Desk, Amazon, Google, premium SSPs, retail ad networks, clean rooms). Secure first-mover advantage on platform alphas and betas, testing them technically and translating them into deployable client solutions.

  • Product-Centric New Business: Architect winning product narratives, bespoke tech architectures, and commercial frameworks for major pitches and RFPs. Lead the programmatic discipline in tier-1 global pitches, driving high pitch-win rates and expanding retained scope.

  • Cross-Discipline Integration: Architect the connective programmatic layer across Search, Social, Retail Media, GEO, and Creative, building unified full-funnel activation frameworks (e.g., audience syncing, cross-channel frequency management, closed-loop attribution).

2. Client Strategic & Technical Leadership (50%)

  • Principal Technical Counsel for Tier-1 Clients: Act as the lead advisor for CMOs, Heads of Media, and MarTech executives at enterprise accounts - translating complex programmatic engineering into board-level growth strategies.

  • Drive Client Programmatic & AI Maturity: Actively advance Tier-1 clients along the programmatic maturity curve.

  • Brief Validation & Technical Governance: Serve as the technical filter on complex client briefs, ensuring brief feasibility and alignment with modern media architectures before execution.

  • Thought Leadership & External Voice: Represent Jellyfish as a category authority through POVs, white papers, analyst briefings, industry summits, and keynotes on topics like cookieless addressability, agentic media buying, and AI-driven curation.

     

Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of advanced programmatic and ad-tech experience within an agency, DSP/SSP, ad-tech vendor, or sophisticated brand-side media team.

  • Expert Technical Proficiency across Enterprise DSPs: Deep technical fluency with platforms such as Display & Video 360 (DV360), The Trade Desk, Amazon DSP, Campaign Manager 360, and major SSP curation tools.

  • Supply Path & Media Economics: Strong track record designing SPO frameworks, private marketplace (PMP) deal structures, and custom algorithm setups.

  • Track Record in Commercial Growth: Proven background contributing to high-value new business pitches, RFPs, and expanding programmatic scope in enterprise brand accounts.

  • No line-management required, but proven leadership through influence, upskilling, and technical mentorship across cross-functional teams.

Note: We emphasise skills, expertise and behavioural attributes over years of experience and traditional degrees. If you want to join our collaborative team, we invite you to apply today with your resume in English.

Additional Information

Join Jellyfish and experience a workplace where we prioritise your growth, celebrate your contributions, and empower you to tailor your work environment to suit your needs.

💰 Reward: You'll be eligible to join our discretionary annual bonus scheme.

💫 Custom Work Environment: Work remotely for up to 60% of your days and shape your day between 8am. and 6:30pm with flexible working hours.

👪 Family Support: Enjoy 14 weeks of paid leave for primary caregivers and 4 weeks of paid leave for secondary caregivers. We also provide £1000 (or equivalent) towards courses for returning primary caregivers to support your transition back into work.

About the Role

The way legal work gets done is changing, and Engagement is at the centre of that transformation. We're looking for an Engagement Manager to join our UK & Ireland Engagement team in London, own adoption across a portfolio of enterprise corporate clients and help some of the world's largest in-house legal functions fundamentally change the way they work.

This is a role for someone who has led change inside large, complex organisations and knows that real transformation is designed and managed. You will own the adoption and long-term success of strategic enterprise accounts: building deep, multi-level relationships, defining the outcomes and serving as the trusted adviser who turns Legora into an embedded part of how those teams operate.

Enterprise means depth: larger, more complex accounts with more revenue at stake. Each account is a global legal function with multiple teams, jurisdictions and business units, its own governance, and a long, multi-phase roadmap. Success depends on navigating that complexity: aligning General Counsel, legal operations, IT, security and procurement, and building momentum one team and one use case at a time until Legora is used across the whole function.

At the heart of the role is designing each client's enterprise adoption strategy and delivering the change programmes that transform how they work. For every account you will build a tailored, multi-year roadmap, sequence initiatives from the first pilot teams to function-wide and global adoption, define measurable outcomes and ROI with executive sponsors, and evolve the programme as new AI capabilities and use cases emerge.

You will be critical as we continue to build a best-in-class enterprise adoption programme at Legora, helping clients realise measurable ROI, expand successful use cases and transform the way their teams work.

What You'll Do

You'll lead the post-sale customer experience, owning onboarding, adoption and long-term value realisation for a portfolio of enterprise accounts. Specifically, you will:

  • Design each client's enterprise adoption strategy: the change-management approach, governance model, stakeholder map across legal, business and IT, and target outcomes for how that legal function adopts Legora.

  • Execute against that strategy, sequencing initiatives from the first pilot teams through to function-wide and global adoption across regions, practice areas and business units.

  • Build and run executive governance with each client, including steering committees, executive business reviews and success plans owned jointly with GC and legal operations leadership.

  • Act as a strategic adviser who deeply understands enterprise in-house legal priorities (cost, cycle time, risk, global consistency and doing more without adding headcount), surfaces high-impact opportunities and guides teams towards maximum value from Legora.

  • Navigate the enterprise landscape, including security reviews, IT and integration requirements, procurement and change-control processes, so that adoption keeps moving.

  • Orchestrate engagement from cross-functional teams to accelerate client success (GTM, Product, Legal Engineering, Engineering, Marketing, Support), keeping full account context and coordination.

  • Partner closely with GTM on renewals, expansion and other key commercial moments, building the case for wider deployment and new use cases across the client's organisation.

  • Turn customer feedback into action by working closely with Product, Engineering and Marketing to shape the roadmap, positioning and enablement for enterprise clients.

  • Build reusable enterprise playbooks, governance templates and enablement material from what works, so the whole Engagement team gets better as you go.

What You Bring

You care deeply about customer outcomes and you know that transformation has to be designed and led. You're proactive, strategic and comfortable steering demanding, senior stakeholders through significant change. You take pride in being the reason customers adopt, grow and succeed.

We're looking for:

  • At least 5 years' experience in management consulting, legal, LegalTech or customer success, ideally with enterprise clients in an AI-native B2B vertical.

  • Experience leading large-scale rollouts and adoption programmes at enterprise or global organisations. We want someone who has taken a new way of working into a large, multi-jurisdictional in-house function, navigated procurement, IT, security and sceptical stakeholders, and made it stick.

  • A consulting or transformation background, with a track record of designing and delivering change-management programmes inside large, matrixed organisations.

  • Experience building multi-year, client-level transformation roadmaps and governance structures, and steering them to measurable outcomes.

  • Confidence engaging C-suite and General Counsel-level stakeholders, running executive reviews and building executive sponsorship.

  • Strong programme management: comfortable running complex, multi-workstream programmes with many stakeholders, dependencies and risks.

  • A track record of driving adoption, retention, expansion and satisfaction with enterprise clients.

  • Experience in legal, compliance or other regulated and complex industries, or the ability to learn a complex domain exceptionally fast.

  • Excellent communication skills, written, verbal and interpersonal. You can hold the room with a General Counsel and roll up your sleeves with the teams who use the product every day.

  • High EQ: you know when to listen, when to advise and when to act.

  • A love of fast-paced, early-stage environments where you help build the playbook, not just follow it.

  • Fluency with metrics, and a focus on data, customer health and outcomes over process.

  • Manager enablement. Equip Advisors to coach managers through people matters. Turn recurring questions into practical guidance and AI-supported resources, equipping managers to take ownership of their decisions.

  • Local policy and process. Close gaps in local policies, playbooks and processes with the relevant owners. Keep guidance current and usable, securing Employee Relations & Compliance approval where required.

  • Jurisdictional readiness. Partner with Employee Relations & Compliance on Advisor certification, training and calibration, addressing gaps in capability and casework quality early.

  • Partnership with People Operations. Give Specialists clear local guidance and escalation routes. Partner on self-service content and workflows so routine requests resolve quickly and judgement-based matters reach Advisors.

  • Local delivery. Coordinate Advisor support for people programs, organisational changes and new markets with People Business Partners, People Programs and Market Expansion.

  • Performance and insights. Use case reviews, service data and feedback to improve quality, response times and manager experience. Share emerging risks and measure the impact of AI and process improvements.


What you'll bring

  • 7+ years in HR generalist, People Advisory or operational HR roles, including leading a team across markets in a growing international company.

  • Strong experience of coaching and advising managers, challenging constructively and overseeing probation, performance and absence cases, with clear judgement on when specialist support is needed.

  • Knowledge of employment practices across multiple jurisdictions, and the ability to work effectively with local experts.

  • A track record of building local HR capability and closing policy and process gaps with practical, usable guidance.

  • Practical experience applying AI to advisory work, knowledge management or case administration, with the ability to test outputs, drive adoption and demonstrate improvements.

  • Comfort working in a tiered People model, with clear boundaries between operations, local advisory, People Business Partners and specialist teams.

  • A hands-on leadership style, strong stakeholder relationships and a high bar for documentation, confidentiality and the quality of advice.

  • Fluency in English, which is our working language.

People Advisory brings local expertise closer to the employees and managers who need it, helping the business move fast with confidence. You will build that capability from the ground up: hiring and developing trusted Advisors across our markets, combining local judgement with consistent standards, and using AI to make expertise easier to access. 2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

  • We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

  • We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

  • We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.


The role
You will establish Legora's first local People Advisory layer, building the team and its capability from the ground up. Reporting to the Director of People Operations, you will define market coverage, lead hiring and onboarding, and develop a distributed team of People Advisors. Your team will provide practical local advice, handle casework and build managers' confidence in handling people matters.

You will establish an AI-first way of working across Advisory: simplifying processes, turning local knowledge into reusable guidance, and using AI to improve preparation, documentation and access to advice.

You will partner with Employee Relations & Compliance on jurisdictional standards, certification and sensitive casework; People Business Partners on local business needs; and People Operations on service delivery. With People Tech & Data, you will turn requirements into reliable tools and workflows for employees and managers.


What you'll own

  • Team build and capability. Establish the Advisory team from the ground up. Coach Advisors towards independent delivery, setting clear expectations for service and judgement.

  • Local advisory delivery. Build a trusted, visible People presence in each market, with Advisors who understand local business needs and build strong relationships with employees and managers.

  • Casework quality and escalation. Oversee probation, performance and absence cases. Ensure clear records and immediate escalation to Employee Relations & Compliance when matters become formal, contested or legally sensitive.

  • Manager enablement. Equip Advisors to coach managers through people matters. Turn recurring questions into practical guidance and AI-supported resources, equipping managers to take ownership of their decisions.

  • Local policy and process. Close gaps in local policies, playbooks and processes with the relevant owners. Keep guidance current and usable, securing Employee Relations & Compliance approval where required.

  • Jurisdictional readiness. Partner with Employee Relations & Compliance on Advisor certification, training and calibration, addressing gaps in capability and casework quality early.

  • Partnership with People Operations. Give Specialists clear local guidance and escalation routes. Partner on self-service content and workflows so routine requests resolve quickly and judgement-based matters reach Advisors.

  • Local delivery. Coordinate Advisor support for people programs, organisational changes and new markets with People Business Partners, People Programs and Market Expansion.

  • Performance and insights. Use case reviews, service data and feedback to improve quality, response times and manager experience. Share emerging risks and measure the impact of AI and process improvements.


What you'll bring

  • 7+ years in HR generalist, People Advisory or operational HR roles, including leading a team across markets in a growing international company.

  • Strong experience of coaching and advising managers, challenging constructively and overseeing probation, performance and absence cases, with clear judgement on when specialist support is needed.

  • Knowledge of employment practices across multiple jurisdictions, and the ability to work effectively with local experts.

  • A track record of building local HR capability and closing policy and process gaps with practical, usable guidance.

  • Practical experience applying AI to advisory work, knowledge management or case administration, with the ability to test outputs, drive adoption and demonstrate improvements.

  • Comfort working in a tiered People model, with clear boundaries between operations, local advisory, People Business Partners and specialist teams.

  • A hands-on leadership style, strong stakeholder relationships and a high bar for documentation, confidentiality and the quality of advice.

  • Fluency in English, which is our working language.

Why this role

People Advisory brings local expertise closer to the employees and managers who need it, helping the business move fast with confidence. You will build that capability from the ground up: hiring and developing trusted Advisors across our markets, combining local judgement with consistent standards, and using AI to make expertise easier to access. It’s an opportunity to shape a new team at one of the most exciting companies in tech and set the standard for how local people support scales globally.

raw.description:
At monday.com, we help teams get more work done. We are the best AI work platform that empowers teams to automate, build, and scale their impact end-to-end with tools that actually execute the work for you. With over $1B in ARR, 250,000+ customers, and a global team, we’re serious about building a product people love to use and giving our employees the same ownership and flexibility to shape the way the world works.

 

We care about the impact you make, not the hours you clock, so we encourage initiative, ownership, and fresh thinking. We back our people with flexible work, wellness and mental health support, and a work environment built on collaboration.

 

We’re currently expanding our engineering teams in London and looking for experienced Tech Leads. This is an individual contributor role with technical leadership scope, it’s not a people management position.

You'll drive the development of infrastructure features that shape our product's future from UI to database.

🎯 Check out our Engineering Blog - https://engineering.monday.com/

 

﻿Please note this is a hybrid role based in our incredible London office in Fitzrovia, with 3 days per week on-site.

About the Team

Our Enterprise Engineering group sits at the heart of monday.com's growth, building the foundational systems that our largest customers depend on. The team is split across two closely connected areas: the Data Lifecycle team, which focuses on data compliance and governance at enterprise scale, and the Account Controls team, which gives internal and external partners the tools to manage and control customer data — and is currently our number one priority for enterprise growth. The work is genuinely complex: you'll be navigating large-scale, cross-product technical challenges, shaping data architecture that touches millions of users, and exploring how AI can be meaningfully applied to data management. Every decision you make has real impact on how enterprise clients experience monday.com. We're a hands-on, collaborative team based in London, working across the full stack (primarily Node.js and React), and we thrive on people who can zoom in on the details when it matters and zoom out to see the bigger picture.

 

About the role:

You'll work with experienced and highly talented engineers who are passionate about what they do, using cutting-edge technologies in a data- and impact-driven environment. We foster a culture of transparency, full ownership, teamwork, and a no-ego policy.

Our engineering department consists of multiple groups, each responsible for a critical domain within the monday.com product. With over 400 engineers, we operate in cross-functional teams, collaboratively defining, improving, building, and delivering features.

What you will do:

  • Play a key in shaping our product architecture and engineering excellence.

  • Evolve our architecture and engineering practices to support the ever-growing scale of users, features, and data.

  • Work alongside experienced and highly skilled developers with cutting-edge technologies.

  • Collaborate closely with Product and Design teams, taking full ownership and responsibility from conception to post-deployment in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

  • Tech stack: React.js, Redux, Node.js, Ruby on Rails, AWS, Elasticsearch, Redis, MySQL.

Note: Prior experience with our tech stack is not required; we welcome people willing to learn.

 

Requirements:

  • 10+ years of experience as a Software Engineer.

  • Strong technical expertise with a proven track record of building products that people love and use daily.

  • Full-stack development experience, with a primary focus on backend.

  • Experience developing large-scale, user-facing web products.

  • Deep product understanding and a passion for creating software that delivers an exceptional user experience.

  • Strong team player with excellent communication skills and empathy.

  • Commitment to quality and simplicity in engineering and product development.

 

What monday.com can offer you:

  • Opportunity to join a well-funded, publicly listed company with big ambitions and strong growth potential.

  • Competitive base salary, bonus, and RSUs.

  • Private healthcare insurance, critical illness, and life insurance coverage.

  • Pension contributions matched up to 7%.

  • ClassPass membership.

  • Buffet breakfast and lunch provided at the office, Monday to Thursday.

  • Fully dedicated learning and development team that provides opportunities for our employees to hone and gain new skills.

  • Fun team events, socials and offsites.

  • Amazing company culture that values transparency and collaboration while never forgetting to have fun while we work! We've been named "Best Place to Work" in the UK.

  • A global, dynamic and passionate environment with employees in Tel Aviv, New York, San Francisco, Miami, Chicago, Denver, London, Warsaw, Sydney, São Paulo, and Tokyo.

raw.title: (Senior) Data Systems Lead
raw.description:
Help us make a big green dent in the universe. We're on a mission to drive the global renewable energy revolution, and we need many more people to help us make our vision a reality. 

Octopus Energy Generation (OEGEN) is a leader in sourcing, investing in, and managing a wide range of utility-scale renewable energy assets. As we continue to expand our investment base, we are dedicated to building a diverse team that reflects the communities we serve. Currently, we manage a global portfolio of over £8 billion in renewable energy assets. 

We are committed to delivering best-in-class responsible investment activity, offering like-minded investors the means and products to invest their capital sustainably. It is our ambition to change the entire energy lifecycle and make every green electron matter, delivering the best outcomes for customers, investors, the environment and society, accelerating the transition to net zero. 

OEGEN Data, Tech & Transformation Team 

We are embarking on a comprehensive transformation program designed to drive significant advancements in our business operations and technology landscape. Our primary goal is to transition from our current reliance on legacy systems and specialized off-the-shelf tools to a more integrated, AI-driven, and data-centric operational model. 

Leveraging insights and guidance from our other technically mature entities like Kraken and OE, we plan to adopt cutting-edge tools and capabilities, particularly in AI and Python-driven solutions. 

By investing in a diverse range of skills, we aim to create a hybrid team capable of operating in both our legacy and future environments, ultimately transforming OEGEN into an efficient, data-driven organization. 

About the role 

The tools are already here. Like the rest of OE Group, OEGEN runs on Databricks, we're moving onto our own Microsoft 365 tenant, and Octopus Energy Group gives us access to a powerful set of shared data and AI capabilities. What we're missing is someone whose job is to make all of it work together for our Fund Management business - and then build genuinely useful things on top of it. 

This is a two-sided role. On one side, you'll integrate: wiring third-party systems, internal apps and document storage into the environment we already have, setting sensible guardrails around access and cost, and adopting existing Group capability wherever it does the job rather than rebuilding it. On the other, you'll build: turning those connections into data products, internal tools and AI-enabled workflows that fund management, asset management and finance use every day. Tying the two together, you'll develop and own the playbook - the documented, repeatable patterns for how a new system gets connected, how a tool gets built and shipped, and how both get supported afterwards - so that what you learn once becomes how the whole team works. The two halves feed each other: you'll understand what's possible because you built the plumbing, and you'll build better plumbing because you know what people actually do with it. 

We want someone with genuine ideas about where AI can take a business like ours, and the pragmatism to ship them. Our team has already built an Excel data mart plugin that puts gold-layer tables directly in the hands of non-technical staff, a metrics taxonomy app that keeps third-party definitions aligned with our own, and AI-assisted workflows that scaffold documentation automatically. There's a long list of things we haven't got to yet. Expect roughly half your time on integration and enablement and half on building, and expect to work closely with the central data platform team so what we do in OEGEN stays consistent with the wider estate and our specific needs get onto their roadmap. 


What You'll Do

  • Integrate the systems our business runs on - third-party providers, internal tools, our own SharePoint and Microsoft 365 tenant - into our existing Databricks environment, via APIs and existing connectors. 

  • Build data products on top of what you connect: well-modelled, documented, reusable datasets that the business consumes directly through Excel, dashboards and natural-language querying, rather than one-off extracts. 

  • Design and ship internal applications and AI-enabled tools - using Python, Streamlit, Databricks Apps (HTMX), Lakebase, FastAPI or similar - that put data and AI directly into the hands of fund management, asset management and finance teams. 

  • Prototype, evaluate and productionise new AI capability, from document AI and retrieval to agentic workflows, and turn the ideas that prove out into supported products rather than abandoned experiments. 

  • Take an adopt-first approach: work with Octopus Energy Group's data platform and AI teams to reuse capability that already exists, and configure it for OEGEN rather than building parallel versions of it. 

  • Set up practical guardrails inside Databricks and Unity Catalog - schema and workspace access, permissions, environment hygiene - so more teams can use it without stepping on each other. 

  • Bring cost management from reactive to proactive: tagging, budgets, alerting and usage monitoring, so Databricks and AI token spend can be attributed to the right team, project or fund before the invoice arrives. 

  • Get our AI usage properly credentialed and logged - managed keys and access rather than API keys sitting in individual password managers - and provide clean patterns for embedding AI into the tools we build. 

  • Standardise how we build and ship internal apps: shared templates, authentication, deployment and documentation, so a tool remains supportable by someone other than the person who wrote it. 

  • Consolidate the ad-hoc scripts, spreadsheets and no-code workflows we've accumulated into fewer, better-understood integrations that don't need babysitting, and automate the repetitive parts of our own workflow. 

  • Work directly with non-technical teams to understand their problems and translate them into things we can build. 


What You'll Need

  • Strong systems integration experience - connecting business systems, SaaS tools and data sources via REST APIs, connectors and authentication flows. 

  • A track record of building and shipping data products or internal applications that people actually use, not just pipelines that feed someone else's reports. 

  • Solid Python and SQL, used daily for building, automation and data modelling. 

  • Hands-on experience with a cloud data platform in production (Databricks preferred): workspaces, catalogs, permissions and compute. 

  • Practical experience integrating AI into real tools - LLM APIs, retrieval, agents - with a clear-eyed sense of what works and what's still a demo. 

  • Practical identity and access experience - SSO, service accounts, credential management and access lifecycle - enough to make sensible, secure choices without a security team holding your hand. 

  • Experience with Microsoft 365 / SharePoint integration, or a comparable enterprise document and collaboration stack. 

  • Real experience keeping cloud or AI usage costs under control: you know what drives the bill and how to attribute and cap it. 

  • A pragmatist's instinct for adopting over building where infrastructure is concerned - you'd rather configure something that exists than write something new - paired with a bias toward shipping when it comes to solutions. 

  • Clear communication. You can explain a trade-off to a fund manager and hold your own in a technical review with a central engineering team. 

  • Comfort with real ownership in a small team, where you set the working patterns rather than inherit them. 


Bonus Points For
 

  • Full-stack or application development experience, particularly with Streamlit, FastAPI or HTMX. 

  • Familiarity with the Databricks ecosystem - Unity Catalog, Databricks Apps, Lakebase, Genie - or equivalent tooling. 

  • Experience with vector search, embeddings, document AI or retrieval-augmented generation in production. 

  • Experience with Terraform, GitHub Actions or similar, to keep configuration version-controlled and repeatable. 

  • FinOps experience: usage monitoring, budgets, showback and chargeback. 

  • Having supported analysts and non-specialist builders using a shared data environment. 

  • Experience in a regulated or audited setting such as financial services, infrastructure investment or energy. 

  • Familiarity with renewable energy, infrastructure investment or financial services data. 

 

  • 💰 Wondering what the salary for this role is? Just ask us! On a call with one of our recruiters it's something we always cover as we genuinely want to match your experience with the correct salary. The reason why we don't advertise is because we honestly have a degree of flexibility and would never want salary to be a reason why someone doesn't apply to Octopus - what's more important to us is finding the right octofit! 

  • 🎉 Octopus Energy Group is a unique culture. An organisation where people learn, decide, and build quicker. Where people work with autonomy, alongside a wide range of amazing co-owners, on projects that break new ground. We want your hard work to be rewarded with perks you actually care about! We were recently named the UK's top company to work for, and we ranked in the top ten in the Sunday Times Best Places to Work 2024. Our Group CEO, Greg has recorded a podcast about our culture and how we empower our people. We've also been placed in the top 10 companies for senior leadership.

Along the way, you'll chat with our recruitment team and your Recruiter will help you throughout different stages. Got any burning questions before then? Drop us a message at ----- and we'd love to help!

raw.description:
Help us make a big green dent in the universe. We're on a mission to drive the global renewable energy revolution, and we need many more people to help us make our vision a reality. 

Octopus Energy Generation (OEGEN) is a leader in sourcing, investing in, and managing a wide range of utility-scale renewable energy assets. As we continue to expand our investment base, we are dedicated to building a diverse team that reflects the communities we serve. Currently, we manage a global portfolio of over £8 billion in renewable energy assets. 

We are committed to delivering best-in-class responsible investment activity, offering like-minded investors the means and products to invest their capital sustainably. It is our ambition to change the entire energy lifecycle and make every green electron matter, delivering the best outcomes for customers, investors, the environment and society, accelerating the transition to net zero. 

OEGEN Data, Tech & Transformation Team 

We are embarking on a comprehensive transformation program designed to drive significant advancements in our business operations and technology landscape. Our primary goal is to transition from our current reliance on legacy systems and specialized off-the-shelf tools to a more integrated, AI-driven, and data-centric operational model. 

Leveraging insights and guidance from our other technically mature entities like Kraken and OE, we plan to adopt cutting-edge tools and capabilities, particularly in AI and Python-driven solutions. 

By investing in a diverse range of skills, we aim to create a hybrid team capable of operating in both our legacy and future environments, ultimately transforming OEGEN into an efficient, data-driven organization. 

About the role 

The tools are already here. Like the rest of OE Group, OEGEN runs on Databricks, we're moving onto our own Microsoft 365 tenant, and Octopus Energy Group gives us access to a powerful set of shared data and AI capabilities. What we're missing is someone whose job is to make all of it work together for our Fund Management business - and then build genuinely useful things on top of it. 

This is a two-sided role. On one side, you'll integrate: wiring third-party systems, internal apps and document storage into the environment we already have, setting sensible guardrails around access and cost, and adopting existing Group capability wherever it does the job rather than rebuilding it. On the other, you'll build: turning those connections into data products, internal tools and AI-enabled workflows that fund management, asset management and finance use every day. Tying the two together, you'll develop and own the playbook - the documented, repeatable patterns for how a new system gets connected, how a tool gets built and shipped, and how both get supported afterwards - so that what you learn once becomes how the whole team works. The two halves feed each other: you'll understand what's possible because you built the plumbing, and you'll build better plumbing because you know what people actually do with it. 

We want someone with genuine ideas about where AI can take a business like ours, and the pragmatism to ship them. Our team has already built an Excel data mart plugin that puts gold-layer tables directly in the hands of non-technical staff, a metrics taxonomy app that keeps third-party definitions aligned with our own, and AI-assisted workflows that scaffold documentation automatically. There's a long list of things we haven't got to yet. Expect roughly half your time on integration and enablement and half on building, and expect to work closely with the central data platform team so what we do in OEGEN stays consistent with the wider estate and our specific needs get onto their roadmap. 


What You'll Do

  • Integrate the systems our business runs on - third-party providers, internal tools, our own SharePoint and Microsoft 365 tenant - into our existing Databricks environment, via APIs and existing connectors. 

  • Build data products on top of what you connect: well-modelled, documented, reusable datasets that the business consumes directly through Excel, dashboards and natural-language querying, rather than one-off extracts. 

  • Design and ship internal applications and AI-enabled tools - using Python, Streamlit, Databricks Apps (HTMX), Lakebase, FastAPI or similar - that put data and AI directly into the hands of fund management, asset management and finance teams. 

  • Prototype, evaluate and productionise new AI capability, from document AI and retrieval to agentic workflows, and turn the ideas that prove out into supported products rather than abandoned experiments. 

  • Take an adopt-first approach: work with Octopus Energy Group's data platform and AI teams to reuse capability that already exists, and configure it for OEGEN rather than building parallel versions of it. 

  • Set up practical guardrails inside Databricks and Unity Catalog - schema and workspace access, permissions, environment hygiene - so more teams can use it without stepping on each other. 

  • Bring cost management from reactive to proactive: tagging, budgets, alerting and usage monitoring, so Databricks and AI token spend can be attributed to the right team, project or fund before the invoice arrives. 

  • Get our AI usage properly credentialed and logged - managed keys and access rather than API keys sitting in individual password managers - and provide clean patterns for embedding AI into the tools we build. 

  • Standardise how we build and ship internal apps: shared templates, authentication, deployment and documentation, so a tool remains supportable by someone other than the person who wrote it. 

  • Consolidate the ad-hoc scripts, spreadsheets and no-code workflows we've accumulated into fewer, better-understood integrations that don't need babysitting, and automate the repetitive parts of our own workflow. 

  • Work directly with non-technical teams to understand their problems and translate them into things we can build. 


What You'll Need

  • Strong systems integration experience - connecting business systems, SaaS tools and data sources via REST APIs, connectors and authentication flows. 

  • A track record of building and shipping data products or internal applications that people actually use, not just pipelines that feed someone else's reports. 

  • Solid Python and SQL, used daily for building, automation and data modelling. 

  • Hands-on experience with a cloud data platform in production (Databricks preferred): workspaces, catalogs, permissions and compute. 

  • Practical experience integrating AI into real tools - LLM APIs, retrieval, agents - with a clear-eyed sense of what works and what's still a demo. 

  • Practical identity and access experience - SSO, service accounts, credential management and access lifecycle - enough to make sensible, secure choices without a security team holding your hand. 

  • Experience with Microsoft 365 / SharePoint integration, or a comparable enterprise document and collaboration stack. 

  • Real experience keeping cloud or AI usage costs under control: you know what drives the bill and how to attribute and cap it. 

  • A pragmatist's instinct for adopting over building where infrastructure is concerned - you'd rather configure something that exists than write something new - paired with a bias toward shipping when it comes to solutions. 

  • Clear communication. You can explain a trade-off to a fund manager and hold your own in a technical review with a central engineering team. 

  • Comfort with real ownership in a small team, where you set the working patterns rather than inherit them. 


Bonus Points For
 

  • Full-stack or application development experience, particularly with Streamlit, FastAPI or HTMX. 

  • Familiarity with the Databricks ecosystem - Unity Catalog, Databricks Apps, Lakebase, Genie - or equivalent tooling. 

  • Experience with vector search, embeddings, document AI or retrieval-augmented generation in production. 

  • Experience with Terraform, GitHub Actions or similar, to keep configuration version-controlled and repeatable. 

  • FinOps experience: usage monitoring, budgets, showback and chargeback. 

  • Having supported analysts and non-specialist builders using a shared data environment. 

  • Experience in a regulated or audited setting such as financial services, infrastructure investment or energy. 

  • Familiarity with renewable energy, infrastructure investment or financial services data.
