raw.title: Product Manager - London
raw.description:
Role summary

We are hiring a Product Manager to own a virtual data room’s (VDR), end to end product strategy: roadmap, requirements, release quality and client outcomes.

You will collaborate with stakeholders, client-facing teams; combining their input with market insight, data and your own judgment to set a clear product direction.

 

What you will do

Strategy and roadmap

  • Own the product vision and roadmap, aligned with TechOps and company goals.

  • Track the VDR market, competitors and emerging technology (especially AI), and turn insight into prioritized bets.

  • Build business cases with cost, revenue and timeline impact, make clear trade-offs, and explain prioritization and scope changes to stakeholders before they ask.

Discovery and requirements

  • Run discovery with clients, deal teams, sales and support to understand real workflows and pain points.

  • Write features and PBIs in Azure DevOps with clear business rules, scope and testable acceptance criteria.

  • Partner with UX design on user-centered solutions for admins, deal managers and external bidders.

 

Delivery and release

  • Work with product, engineering and QA to plan sprints, unblock work and keep releases moving.

  • Be the first point of contact for product questions from engineering, QA and UX.

  • Own release readiness, UAT and release notes for every release, including hotfixes.

  • Triage escalations and client-reported issues, and agree priorities with Support.

 

Measurement and clients

  • Define and track product metrics (adoption, time to set up a room, retention, NPS, incident and defect trends), and use product analytics to judge feature performance and guide prioritization.

  • Present to key clients and partners, and support sales on high-value deals.


What you bring

  • Hands-on virtual data room experience as a product manager, product owner, VDR administrator or heavy deal-side user.

  • 3+ years as a Product Manager, Product Owner or similar role on B2B SaaS.

  • A track record of writing clear requirements and acceptance criteria that engineering and QA can build and test from.

  • Experience running agile delivery with Azure DevOps, Jira, Confluence or similar, including release planning and UAT.

  • Working understanding of security and compliance requirements in enterprise software.

  • Data-driven decision making, with experience using product analytics to measure what works.

  • Strong written and spoken English; you explain technical topics clearly to business stakeholders.

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

 

Nice to have

  • Background in M&A, investment banking, legal or corporate development.

  • Experience shipping AI features such as document classification, search, summarization or automated redaction.

  • Experience working in a distributed team across time zones.

  • Familiarity with web technologies and APIs.

  • Experience with multilingual products or localization.

  • Additional languages.

The role

We are formalising our security assurance function. We have technical controls and the engineering culture; what we need now is the governance layer that proves it - to our auditors, to our funders, and to our regulator.

You will be the delivery engine behind that. You will own the recurring assurance cycle end to end, run our third-party security programme, and be the person who turns evidence into something a due diligence team or a certification auditor can be satisfied by.

You will be responsible for building controls, gathering evidence, and challenging suppliers.

What you will own:

1. Third-party security assurance

- Run security due diligence on new suppliers, maintain initial questionnaire to risk sign-off, working with Procurement and Legal on security and data protection schedules.

- Maintain a supplier tiering model based on criticality and run the periodic re-assessment cycle for tiered suppliers: certification expiry, subprocessor changes, breach notifications, SLA performance.

- Maintain the supplier and outsourcing registers, including preparation for the FCA's material third party register under PS26/2 (rules in force 18 March 2027).

- Track concentration risk and exit plans for critical suppliers.

2. Inbound due diligence and customer assurance

- Own our response to security due diligence from funders, banking partners, institutional investors, commercial partners and prospects.

- Build and maintain a reusable trust pack: answer library, security whitepaper, current certifications, pen test attestations, standard questionnaire pre-fills (SIG, CAIQ).

- Turn a 40-hour bespoke questionnaire response into a 4-hour one.

3. The assurance calendar

- Maintain the annual calendar of security activities and make sure each one happens, produces evidence, and closes its actions: penetration tests, access reviews, disaster recovery tests, tabletop exercises, policy reviews, supplier re-assessments, awareness training.

- Coordinate external penetration tests: scoping, vendor selection, scheduling, findings triage, remediation tracking, retest.

- Facilitate tabletop exercises, including scenario design and post-exercise action tracking.

4. Risk and control administration

- Maintain the information security risk register: run the assessment cycle, record treatment plans with named owners and dates, chase closure.

- Administer the policy exception and risk acceptance process, ensuring every exception is owned, time-bound and reviewed on expiry.

- Perform first-line control testing: sample-test where key controls operate as designed and retain the evidence.

- Produce security MI for the Head of Security to take to ExCo and the Risk Committee.

5. Vulnerability and findings management

- Consolidate findings across sources — EDR, cloud security posture, SAST/DAST/SCA, secrets scanning, penetration tests — into a single view with agreed severity definitions and remediation SLAs.

- Triage, route and chase remediation with engineering teams; escalate ageing findings.

- Own the reporting on remediation performance.

6. Security awareness

- Run the awareness programme: induction, annual refresher, phishing simulation, role-based training for engineers, completion tracking.

- Coordinate pre-employment screening with People.

What you will contribute to:

- The ISO 27001 ISMS, which we are building towards certification. You will draft and maintain control documentation, populate the Statement of Applicability, gather evidence, coordinate the internal audit programme and be a primary point of contact for our external auditor. The Head of Security owns the framework, scope, and risk appetite.

- Policies and standards: you will draft, review and shepherd policies through approval, and track the review cycle.

- Incident response: you will maintain the IR plan and playbooks, facilitate post-incident reviews, track remediation actions, and support regulatory notification (ICO personal data breach reporting within 72 hours; FCA notification under Principle 11 / SUP 15.3).

- Business continuity and DR: you will maintain the documentation and the testing evidence.

- Secure development: you will help embed security requirements into the SDLC and support threat modelling sessions.

- Data protection: you will support RoPA maintenance, DPIA completion and DSAR handling alongside Legal.

What success looks like:

First 90 days: you know our supplier estate and have tiered it; the assurance calendar for the next 12 months is published and owned; inbound due diligence requests come to you and go out without the Head of Security rewriting them.

Six months: the trust pack exists and is being used; the risk register is live with owned treatment plans; ISO 27001 evidence collection is systematic rather than a scramble; the exception register exists.

Twelve months: supplier re-assessment runs on a cadence without prompting; the material third party register is ready ahead of the March 2027 deadline; MI to the Risk Committee is trusted.

Essential experience:

- Three or more years in an information security assurance, GRC or security compliance role, at least some of it in a regulated financial services environment or another environment with real external audit pressure.

- Hands-on experience of ISO 27001, whether operating an ISMS or taking one through certification.

- Demonstrable experience running third-party or vendor security assessments, and of responding to inbound security due diligence.

- Comfortable reading technical findings — an EDR vulnerability report, a penetration test finding, a cloud misconfiguration — and forming your own view on severity and real-world exploitability rather than passing the vendor's rating through unchanged.

- Clear, concise written English. Much of this role is writing things that external parties will judge us on.

- The confidence to chase a busy engineer, challenge a supplier's assertion, and tell us when an answer is not good enough.

Desirable:

- Experience of a cloud-native environment, ideally AWS.

- Experience of scaling a control framework as an organisation grows.

- Familiarity with UK operational resilience expectations (SYSC 15A) and outsourcing requirements (SYSC 8).

- Certifications such as CISM, CISA, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor, CRISC or CCSP. We care more about what you have done than what you hold.

The Role

We are hiring a Product Lead to own our Express / Mid-prime personal loan product, one of our highest-priority growth areas. This is unsecured personal lending in the higher-APR mid-prime space (30% to 50% APR), with loans typically from £2,000 to £10,000, and customers acquired primarily through price-comparison and aggregator marketplaces. Our ambition is to grow this product many times over while improving its economics, and this role owns the product that makes that happen.

This is a product role first. You will own the Express/Mid-prime proposition end to end: who we serve, how we quote and present offers on marketplaces, how the journey converts, how we price, and how the product performs once the loans are on the book. What makes it different from a typical product role is that the product is credit. The levers that drive growth, such as eligibility, pricing, offer design and underwriting, are the same levers that drive loss rates, so you need to be comfortable working with risk and data science rather than handing that part off.

We think this is a great role for someone with around four to five years of experience who has built a strong foundation in lending or fintech, has worked hands-on with data and credit decisioning, and is ready to own a product outright rather than a slice of one. You will set the direction for the segment, run the roadmap, and be accountable for the results, with the backing of experienced risk, data science and commercial leaders around you.

Our decisioning is built on Open Banking and cashflow underwriting rather than credit scores alone. For a higher-APR population acquired through marketplaces, seeing real affordability is what lets us select and price better than the market. The interesting product problem is that richer data comes at a cost to conversion, so the job is to capture that data advantage while designing a journey and offer that customers actually complete.

The defining challenge is balance: scaling volume by an order of magnitude while building a book of genuinely good credit quality. The best people in this space know that those two goals can be reconciled rather than traded off, and are curious enough to work out how.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the Express / Mid-prime product: proposition, roadmap, performance and economics, with direct accountability for the balance between growth and credit quality.

  • Lead how we quote and present offers across aggregator and price-comparison marketplaces, optimising eligibility, risk-based pricing and offer presentation to win the right customers at the point of acquisition.

  • Own conversion through the journey, from quote to disbursal, including how we ask customers for Open Banking data and how that affects drop-off and the quality of the book.

  • Understand and actively manage adverse selection in marketplace-acquired lending, shaping offer, pricing and decisioning strategy to attract the customers we want and screen out the risk we do not.

  • Work with data science to make sure our credit models are calibrated and tuned for this population rather than inherited unchanged from prime or adjacent segments, and be able to get into the data yourself when needed.

  • Use credit and commercial insight to optimise unit economics, balancing approval rates, pricing, loss rates and volume so the product scales profitably.

  • Monitor product and portfolio performance across the customer lifecycle, spotting emerging trends, risks and opportunities early.

  • Shape underwriting strategy, segmentation, credit policy and decisioning logic in partnership with risk and data science.

  • Design and evaluate experiments and strategy changes, and turn the analysis into clear, actionable recommendations.

  • Own the management information for the segment: define the metrics, monitoring and reporting that let the business make consistent decisions about the product.

  • Assess new initiatives, customer segments and product changes with both a commercial and a credit lens.

  • Present clear, structured updates on product performance to senior leadership and governance forums, and support funding and due diligence conversations where the product is in focus.

We're building the AI operating system that absorbs this complexity and gives enterprises back their speed. Major enterprises already trust us with their most critical systems. We've closed game-changing SI partnerships, just raised a $60M Series A, and demand is outpacing what we can service.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. We care more about trajectory and sharpness than a perfect match.

About the role

We're looking for a Customer Trust Specialist to join our London office and help run the customer-facing side of our trust program. Where our GRC team keeps the compliance engine running behind the scenes, you'll be one of the people customers actually interact with, turning our security, privacy, and AI-governance posture into accurate answers that earn trust. You'll handle security questionnaires end to end, help operate our trust automation platform, and support customer conversations across EMEA and beyond. This is a great fit for someone with solid security-review experience who wants to grow their scope at a fast-scaling AI company.

What you'll do

  • Handle security questionnaires end to end: intake, drafting, review, and delivery for customer security assessments, RFPs, and vendor evaluations, in whatever format they arrive (OneTrust, spreadsheets, portals, email), pulling in Security, Legal, or Engineering when an answer needs it.

  • Operate our trust automation platform: use and help improve the system that generates answers from our governed knowledge base. Review output for accuracy, flag weak or incorrect answers, and help keep the guardrails from over-claiming.

  • Keep the knowledge base current: update answers as the platform, certifications, and control environment change; ingest new evidence (SOC 2, ISO 27001/27701/42001, HIPAA, penetration tests); and flag stale facts before they reach a customer.

  • Handle one-off customer requests: evidence requests, Trust Center access, point questions from account teams, and anything that doesn't fit a questionnaire but still shapes a customer's confidence.

  • Support customer calls: join prospect and customer calls alongside Sales and Solutions to field security, privacy, and AI-safety questions, especially for UK and EMEA customers. Partner with the sales team from intake through close.

  • Support contract reviews: work with Legal and Deal Desk on security and privacy terms in DPAs and MSAs, including UK GDPR and EU data-transfer questions; learn which positions are standard and which need escalation.

  • Keep the program honest: follow the standing rules that protect us and our customers: state only our standard position, never reference another customer's ask or situation, and escalate anything that needs Legal, Security, or Engineering sign-off.

  • Track program data: log knowledge-base gaps, recurring questions we can't answer well yet, and where automation is saving or costing time, and share findings with the team.

  • Help maintain public trust artifacts: keep the Trust Center, security whitepapers, and supporting evidence current and aligned with what we actually do.

How the role will grow

raw.description:
About Griffin

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The team

Griffin is a UK bank built for builders. We give fintechs and platforms the bank accounts and payment rails to launch their own financial products, and clients like Uber, Yonder, Anna Money and Counting Up build on us. Our commercial team brings sales, customer success and marketing together to win, onboard and grow those clients. We’re a team of 10 people, made up of former founders and growth specialists.

The opportunity

You’ll become the engine behind how our commercial team makes decisions. Working alongside the Chief Revenue Officer, the Head of Commercial and the Head of Marketing, you’ll see the full picture of how a bank wins, onboards and grows its clients, and your analysis will shape where the team focuses next. There’s no narrow lane here. One week you’re building a forecast, the next you’re preparing a renewal review, and if something needs an owner, it’s yours.

What success looks like

In your first 6 months, you’ll have given the commercial team a forecast it trusts and spotted risks early, so every quarter end runs smoothly. People across Sales, Customer Success and Marketing will rely on our data because it’s accurate and up to date, and the team’s reviews will run like clockwork. The board and investors will receive numbers they can follow with confidence, and the executive team will already be turning to you for its priority projects.

To do this you’ll own

  • The numbers: the reporting that runs our commercial business, from pipeline and bookings to annual recurring revenue (ARR), net revenue retention and consumption against forecast, plus pricing and deal-structure modelling, including consumption-based pricing and customer profitability

  • Our CRM: clean, well-structured data, built with Sales and Customer Success around clear stage definitions and fields people actually use

  • Sales and customer success insight: analysis of conversion, sales cycle length, win and loss reasons and pipeline coverage, plus account analysis for renewals covering volumes, revenue, margin and product adoption

  • Marketing performance: campaign tracking and pipeline attribution so every pound of spend ties back to revenue, alongside ad hoc work like target account lists and event reporting

  • Commercial governance: deal approval and discount policies, pricing and contract records and clear audit trails, working with Legal, Compliance and Finance

  • Our operating cadence: documented processes and the weekly, monthly and quarterly reviews that keep the team in rhythm

  • Executive projects: high-priority projects, briefings and materials that give you close exposure to how strategic decisions get made

We expect you to shape this role

This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that’s for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background

To ensure this, we’re looking for people who have most of the following:

  • You’ll have some experience as an operator. If it’s in a commercial, revenue operations, sales operations, analytics, consulting or finance role then that’s a bonus

  • A habit of rolling up your sleeves and taking ownership without waiting to be asked

  • Curiosity about fintech, banking and how money moves

  • A structured mind and an eye for detail, with the flexibility to switch between spreadsheets, research and talking to people, and a knack for finding the story in the numbers and explaining it simply

  • The ability to learn quickly, ask good questions and take feedback well

  • A love of writing - we have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write)

Ideally, you would also:

  • Have experience in fintech, SaaS or a fast-growing startup

  • Want to build a career in commercial, sales or growth

How do I apply?

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

We don’t work with recruitment agencies, so please don’t send us speculative CVs.

Under representation

At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

raw.description:
About Lendable

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

  • One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

  • Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

  • Profitable since 2017

  • Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

  • Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot)

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role

We're looking for a proactive, data-driven Associate Product Manager to join our UK Loans product team. You'll play an important role in shaping the customer experience after they take out a loan: from how we engage with customers and manage payments, to how we support those who experience financial difficulty.

APMs at Lendable take ownership of their product changes, working closely with teams across Engineering, Credit, Finance and Operations to solve problems and take the business to the next level.

You'll have the opportunity to solve complex problems, scale impactful products, and help shape the future of our lending experience. If you're excited by fintech and enjoy turning data and customer insight into great products, we'd love to hear from you.

What you’ll work on

  • Improving repayment performance: Running experiments to help more customers pay on time, from choosing repayment dates to how and when we remind people to pay.

  • Personalising customer engagement: Own how we communicate across email, SMS and in-app notifications, testing new messages and improving our tooling.

  • Making loan management easier: Optimising and expanding journeys within the Zable SuperApp, particularly for those who need additional financial support.

  • Using data to drive improvements: Work with Credit and Data Science to identify opportunities and build models to improve payment and servicing outcomes. Build dashboards to track key metrics and measure the impact of what we launch.

  • Testing and learning with customers: Running customer research and testing ideas to understand what people need, how they behave and what works best.

  • Taking products from idea to launch: Working across Engineering, Data Science and Operations to understand the impact of new features, coordinate their rollout and make sure they work for both customers and the business.

  • Increasing impact with AI: Building tools and automations with AI that save time for you, the ops team and the wider business

What we're looking for

Don't worry if you don't meet every single one of the criteria. We'd love to hear from great candidates who are curious, proactive and excited to learn.

  • Experience: 1–2 years in product, or 2-3 years in strategy, analytics, consulting or similar roles, ideally with experience working closely with product or delivery teams to get things done.

  • Communication: You can clearly explain ideas and requirements to different audiences, from writing specs for engineers to training Operations teams.

  • Curiosity: You ask lots of questions and aren't satisfied until you understand why something is happening.

  • Problem-solving: You enjoy forming hypotheses and finding the quickest way to test them, even if the first version is rough around the edges.

  • Data-driven: You're comfortable working with data and can use SQL or Python to investigate problems and answer your own questions.

  • AI-native: You're already experimenting with AI tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex in your work or side projects, and are excited to see how far they can take you.

  • Hands-on: You're happy to roll up your sleeves and pick up the small jobs. In a lean product team, no task is beneath your attention.

  • Adaptable: You enjoy variety and like that no two days look quite the same.

  • Bonus: Experience in lending, payments, fintech or a fast-growing startup.

AI at Lendable

We want to build the most AI-forward financial services company in the world. PMs here make their own dashboards to answer questions that used to need an analyst, build their own agents and workflows to take care of repetitive work, and ship straightforward changes to production themselves. You don't need to be an expert on day one, but we'll expect you to keep pushing what one person can do.

Interview process

  • A quick chat with someone from our Product team to see if the role is a good match

  • A 15 minute cognitive assessment

  • A take home task; a practical product challenge to complete in your own time

  • Task debrief with the product team

  • Final round (in our London office) - typically with the CPO and UK Loans MD, Engineering Manager, Head of Product and hiring manager

Location

This position is a hybrid role based in London, please note we're unable to provide sponsorship for this position

Life at Lendable

  • Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

  • Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

  • Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbeing, including private health cover

As Head of Compliance Monitoring, you'll own Lendable's risk-based compliance monitoring programme and lead the team that delivers it. You'll provide independent second line assurance that the business meets its legal and regulatory obligations, and evidence the outcomes customers actually receive rather than the processes behind them.

You'll report to the Head of Compliance (SMF 16, Compliance Oversight) and deputise for them, including at Board meetings and sub-committees. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who has built a second line monitoring function in a UK FCA regulated consumer credit firm and wants the autonomy to shape one in a fast-growing fintech. The role is not itself a Senior Manager Function.

  • Test the design and operating effectiveness of first line controls, and provide second line assurance over first line quality assurance

  • Issue clear, evidence-based reports setting out findings, root cause, risk ratings and owned actions, then track remediation to closure and validate that it worked

  • Escalate actual or potential customer harm promptly, and assess it for redress and for notification to the FCA under Principle 11 and SUP 15

  • Produce monitoring MI for the Head of Compliance, executive management and the Board, and present it at committees

  • Support FCA supervisory engagement, information requests and skilled person (s166) reviews, and coordinate coverage with Internal Audit, Risk and first line QA

  • Bring data protection into scope, testing UK GDPR and DPA 2018 compliance alongside the Data Protection Officer

  • Lead, coach and develop the compliance monitoring team, planning resource against the plan and building capability through data, analytics and better tooling

What we’re looking for

  • Demonstrable compliance monitoring experience within a UK FCA regulated firm, including designing, owning and delivering a risk-based compliance monitoring programme

  • Experience of leading, managing and developing a team

  • Consumer credit experience, with a strong working knowledge of CONC and the Consumer Credit Act

  • Strong working knowledge of the FCA Handbook, in particular PRIN and the Consumer Duty, SYSC, DISP and SMCR, and of FCA expectations of a second line monitoring function

  • Data protection knowledge, covering the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018

  • Ability to write clear, concise, evidence-based reports and to present findings credibly to senior management, the Board and its committees

  • Sound judgement and personal resilience, with the independence and confidence to challenge the business constructively and to escalate where necessary

  • Strong planning and organisational skills, with the ability to deliver a plan across competing priorities

Highly desirable

  • Internal audit experience gained in a third line function, and/or a relevant professional qualification (for example IIA, ICA or CISI)

  • Secured lending experience, from either a second or third line perspective, including knowledge of MCOB

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role

We're building a larger, dedicated Platform team at Lendable, increasing our investment in the infrastructure that enables our products and engineering teams to scale.

We're hiring a Technical Product Manager to sit within Engineering and connect platform technology, reliability and commercial value. You'll own what we prioritise and why, giving engineers the business context they need while helping Product and leadership understand the impact and opportunities that Platform enables.

This is a hands-on technical IC role, where you'll stay close to engineering through writing code, reviewing PRs and contributing to architecture discussions.

Working closely with the Platform Engineering Manager and Tech Lead, you'll help shape the Platform roadmap, connect technical investment to measurable business outcomes, and build the foundations that allow Lendable to move faster and scale with confidence.

What you'll be doing

Own platform stability

  • Own platform stability as a primary accountability - SLA/SLO metrics, incident rates, release quality.

  • Hold release gating authority: block features from production that don't meet testing standards or introduce unacceptable regression risk.

  • Enforce CI/CD standards centrally so pods don't fragment into one-off solutions.

  • Track and report stability metrics alongside commercial outcomes - stability is the foundation that makes the rest possible.

Be commercially accountable

  • Own the business case for platform investment and answer "why are we spending six engineers on this for three months?" in terms leadership understands.

  • Track platform impact in business terms: developer velocity, incident cost, time-to-market, reliability, capacity - e.g. "CXO rollout removes a 3-second API fan-out, reducing session abandonment" or "we can now handle 20k simultaneous logins".

  • Input into headcount and investment decisions for the platform team.

Own the platform roadmap

  • Own the platform backlog, prioritised by business value and sequenced to unblock the highest-value product teams first - not driven by technical debt or engineer preference alone.

  • Make trade-offs explicit: "if we do X now, we defer Y by Z weeks - here's what that means for products depending on us".

  • Ensure every initiative has a defined success metric that non-engineers can track.

Be the stakeholder interface

  • Act as the single point of contact for Pod Leads: business requirements coming from pods and engineering/developer requirements flowing to pods; prioritise both in service of platform stability.

  • Make platform work visible to leadership - regular forums with product MDs and PMs to capture upcoming dependencies before they become blockers; represent platform work in leadership reviews; translate technical milestones into business milestones.

  • Drive cross-team collaboration and buy-in with other PMs; engage architecture in technical design.

  • Escalate when product teams make requests that would create unsustainable platform load or technical debt.

Contribute as an engineer

  • Write code, review PR's, and participate in architecture design as a core part of the role - not a side project.

  • Bring a strong technical voice to roadmap decisions without owning final architecture calls (that's Architecture and Tech Leads).

What we're looking for

Essential

  • Deep, hands-on engineering background - this role must be staffed by someone who has shipped production systems, not someone who has only managed backlogs.

  • Strong commercial instinct: can build a business case, speak to P&L impact, and hold a line on ROI.

  • Exceptional stakeholder management across product, engineering, and finance without direct line authority over all of them.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity - platform value is often indirect and long-horizon.

  • Track record of contributing as an IC while operating at a senior, cross-team level.

  • Proactive, low-ego, and clear communicator - able to hold a line with leadership and pod leads alike.

Nice to have

  • Experience in platform, infrastructure, or developer tooling contexts.

  • Familiarity with SLA/SLO frameworks and incident management at scale.

  • Experience enforcing CI/CD standards across multiple teams or pods.

  • Prior work making "invisible" infrastructure legible to non-technical leadership.

Our tech stack

Platform & backend: Kotlin, AWS, Postgres, RabbitMQ, Docker, Kubernetes.

Gateway & clients: Node GraphQL gateway, React Native / TypeScript mobile app, Relay.

Tooling & observability: GitHub, GitHub Actions, Jira, Confluence, Datadog, Sentry, Grafana.

Interview process

  • Quick call with the Talent Team (30 minutes)

  • Hiring manager interview (30 minutes)

  • Technical and Product interview (90 minutes)

  • Culture-add interview (60 minutes)

Life at Lendable

  • Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

raw.description:
TL;DR — We're seeking an exceptional Brand Designer to own the visual direction and craft of our website. You'll shape how Lovable looks, feels and communicates online - working closely with design engineering and marketing to turn ideas into world-class web experiences.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.


What we're looking for

  • 7+ years of experience, with a portfolio of shipped websites that demonstrate strong visual craft and brand thinking

  • Portfolio showing landing pages, brand systems, or marketing sites where design decisions clearly serve the story (if your portfolio is mostly product/UI work - check out our other roles)

  • A sharp eye for typography, layout, color, and motion, with the taste to know what's on-brand and what isn't

  • Comfort designing directly for the web - you think in real breakpoints, real type scales, and real constraints, not just static comps

  • Ability to systematise creative choices in design systems - contributing to a shared design system across both product and brand

  • Experience partnering closely with design engineers to get explorations into production without losing the soul of the idea

  • You’re no stranger to shipping your own designs directly to production - perhaps with a little help from AI

  • Ideally - you've got a point of view on where web design is headed and aren't afraid to push for something unexpected

  • We’re prioritising candidates based in London or Stockholm, or willing to relocate


What you'll do

In one sentence: Own the visual and brand craft of Lovable's website, making sure every page feels unmistakably Lovable.

  • Design landing pages, campaign sites, and web experiences that make people stop scrolling

  • Set and evolve the visual language for lovable.dev - typography, layout systems, imagery, motion principles

  • Pair closely with design engineering to translate explorations into scalable, web-native implementations, staying involved through to shipped pixels

  • Collaborate with marketing and brand to make sure the website tells the right story at the right moment - launches, campaigns, positioning shifts

  • Build and maintain a visual system that keeps the site consistent while leaving room for creative surprises

  • Bring a strong opinion on craft and hold the line on quality, even under deadline pressure

  • Help define what "world-class" looks like for marketing sites

How we hire

  1. Fill in a short form then jump on an intro call with a recruiter.

  2. Show us some of your work you're really proud of.

  3. Walk us through your process and craft across several design interviews.

  4. In some cases, we may opt to do paid, trial work.

About your application

  • Please submit your application in English — it's our company language so you'll be speaking lots of it if you join

  • We treat all candidates equally — if you're interested please apply through our careers portal

raw.description:
Metaview is an AI company focused on recruiting. We build AI agents that help world-class companies hire with radically more speed and precision. We automate the toil, and augment the human for companies like Brex, Affirm, Deel, ElevenLabs, and Airtable.

Founded by Siadhal and Shahriar after their experiences scaling Uber and Palantir, we’ve raised $110m from top-tier investors including Google Ventures and Insight Partners.

It’s still day 0: Now is the time to re-engineer how work gets done with AI at the core, and our toughest challenges still lie ahead. We’re looking for people seeking the hardest, most fulfilling work of their lives.

 

How we work

We operate with one core principle: velocity. In practice, this means we:

  • Optimize everything we do around accelerating rate of learning.

  • Do truly great work

  • Communicate openly and directly, and with full context.

All while maintaining a hard-earned reputation for craft and quality.

 

The role:

We’re at an exciting inflection point: strong customer love, clear product–market fit, and accelerating growth. As our GTM Recruiter, you’ll partner directly with GTM leadership to build a world-class commercial organization. You’ll own the full GTM recruiting lifecycle with an emphasis on Sales, while also building on the foundational systems, processes, and tools that will scale our hiring engine. All while working within the business operating at the bleeding edge of how hiring gets done with AI.

Key ownership areas:

  • Partner with the Co-founder/CEO and GTM leaders to define hiring needs across Sales, CS, and Marketing.

  • Own end-to-end recruiting for GTM roles: sourcing, outreach, screening, stakeholder alignment, interviews, and offer processes.

  • Refine our recruiting infrastructure and keep making it sharper.

    • The bigger opportunity: build a hiring machine that combines systematic rigour with human judgement; 100x'ing our capacity and leaving the competition at the starting line.

  • Develop genuine expertise in GTM talent markets. Where the best operators are, what they care about, what it takes to land them.

  • Keep leadership honest. Surface pipeline realities and translate them into clear, data-driven decisions, trade-offs, and next steps.

 

What you bring:

  • 3+ years in full-cycle recruiting at a fast-paced, high-growth B2B startup (experience hiring for GTM roles desirable)

  • A skilled assessor with an unusually high bar for talent. You can assess the intangibles that separate exceptional candidates from competent ones, and sell the opportunity in the same breath.

  • A network, or the hunger and discipline to build one fast. You know where the best GTM operators are, what they care about, and how to get their attention.

  • AI-native. You've already figured out how to use it to move faster and hire better. You're not waiting for permission or a playbook.

  • Comfortable partnering directly with founders and GTM leaders. You can push back, hold the line on bar, and earn trust doing both.

  • A hunter mentality. The GTM talent market doesn't give up its best people easily. You'll find a way.

 

What we offer:

  • The best co-workers you’ll ever have, in an environment that fosters cohesion, collaboration, and performance.

  • Supreme rate-of-learning as we re-orient how the world works with AI.

  • High compensation, through cash and equity.

  • All the benefits you’d expect and more.

raw.description:
About Motorway

Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding.

This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better.

Senior Manager, Coach & Instructor Enablement

FTC 14 months

Coach & Instructor Enablement exists to make the delivery organisation measurably better at retaining learners and delivering successful outcomes consistently, predictably and at scale.

You will enhance our existing strategy and lead the team through its exciting next stage of growth. The team will form around four capability pillars and a new Enablement Operations platform. You will be building that structure while it delivers across a large delivery organisation that supports thousands of learners. Priorities will shift underneath you as delivery data moves, and part of the job is deciding what starts, what stops, and most importantly what must not slip.

This is a role for a strong operator who excels at influencing and collaborating across complex teams and departments. A proven track record of getting work done across teams with clear asks, embedding shared measures of success, and creating an environment where there is no ambiguity about who owns what is are the keys to success within this role.

You will lead a team of six specialists supporting hundreds of coaches and instructors across all learner programmes.

What you'll own

  • Delivery Fundamentals: the standard for what good coaching and instruction look like, QA against that standard, calibration in partnership with Delivery and Quality

  • Operational & Regulatory Change: every coach and instructor has the process, tooling and regulatory knowledge to deliver, and gets it before the change reaches a learner.

  • Technical Skills & Programme Requirements: coaches and instructors are current and designated on the technical content they deliver.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and develop six specialists through regular 1:1s, feedback, and clear individual measures.

Skills & Qualifications

raw.title: AI Engineer
raw.description:
About us

People assume the supply chain is an automated, algorithmic system. It is not. It is a large number of people acting as the glue between organisations and systems, doing work the world depends on with tools that have barely changed in decades. Nexcade builds AI agents for those people, starting in freight forwarding, a $210BN industry.

Our agents are live in production with some of the leading global forwarders, pricing millions in freight every week, and we are expanding the platform deeper into the shipment lifecycle. We have raised $8.5M to make this a reality.

Our founders, Dan and Tasho, spent years at Sedna and Palantir working with supply chain companies on problems like this one. We are backed by top VCs and angels who backed or founded Synthesia, n8n and other world-class companies.

 

How we work

  • Everybody codes, founders included. The whole company is technical, commercial team included, and runs on coding agents.

  • Closely with customers and design partners, so what we ship changes how they operate.

  • At pace. Fast cycles and quick iterations, on the product and on how we work.

  • End to end. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom (and the responsibility) to fix it.

  • In person, 4+ days a week in London. We value synchronous communication.

  • Debate rigorously, decide quickly, execute relentlessly.

  • Enjoy the journey. Hard problems, good colleagues.

     

The role

We are building the AI platform for freight forwarding and expanding our product surface, and we are hiring software engineers across product, AI and platform to do it.

You will build products that do freight forwarding work alongside our customers' teams, operating across the entire shipment lifecycle. You will work across the stack in Python, TypeScript and React, and directly with customers and founders on what gets built.

Everyone here works across the stack, but each engineer has a spike: the area where they set the bar for the team. You spend most of your time where yours is, and lean on your colleagues where theirs are.

  • Product: You build best in class products for the core jobs in freight forwarding, one job at a time. You work as a design partner with our customers to understand the work deeply, turn that understanding into a product they would choose over anything else, and feed what you learn back into the platform everyone builds on.

  • AI: You raise the ceiling on what our AI can do and the floor on how reliably it does it. That spans high volume tasks like classification and extraction and deep workflow tasks that run for hours. You design for performance, reliability, explainability and control, set up the gyms and evals to measure them, and build the harness that runs our agents in all of our products.

  • Platform: You own the foundation every product stands on: the runtime for thousands of concurrent agents and workflows, the way they communicate and scale, the controls for how they access data with permissions that hold, and the observability to see and measure all of it. You ensure the rest of the team can move fast without fear.

     

What we look for

  • A spike, with evidence. Something you have been exceptional at and proof of it. We hire on slope rather than years, so there is no experience threshold in either direction.

  • Strong fundamentals. In the AI-assisted era, having good technical judgement is key. You have shipped production systems people depend on, seen them fail and learned from it.

  • High agency and ownership. You take an ambiguous problem, make a call, and see it through.

  • Humility and learning velocity. You want to get better and you change your mind when the evidence says so.

  • Interest in the problem. You do not need a freight background, but you need to find messy real-world operations interesting rather than a chore.

     

Why join

You will shape the product, the architecture and the company, working alongside an engineering team from Palantir, Raft, Faculty, UnlikelyAI and Oxford. You will work directly with the businesses using what you build, on AI applied to an industry that has resisted software for decades. You will get meaningful equity, so when this works you share in it.

Nexcade builds AI agents for those people, starting in freight forwarding, a $210BN industry.

Our agents are live in production with some of the leading global forwarders, pricing millions in freight every week, and we are expanding the platform deeper into the shipment lifecycle. We have raised $8.5M to make this a reality.

Our founders, Dan and Tasho, spent years at Sedna and Palantir working with supply chain companies on problems like this one. We are backed by top VCs and angels who backed or founded Synthesia, n8n and other world-class companies.

 

How we work

  • Everybody codes, founders included. The whole company is technical, commercial team included, and runs on coding agents.

  • Closely with customers and design partners, so what we ship changes how they operate.

  • At pace. Fast cycles and quick iterations, on the product and on how we work.

  • End to end. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom (and the responsibility) to fix it.

  • In person, 4+ days a week in London. We value synchronous communication.

  • Debate rigorously, decide quickly, execute relentlessly.

  • Enjoy the journey. Hard problems, good colleagues.

     

The role

We are building the AI platform for freight forwarding and expanding our product surface, and we are hiring software engineers across product, AI and platform to do it.

You will build products that do freight forwarding work alongside our customers' teams, operating across the entire shipment lifecycle. You will work across the stack in Python, TypeScript and React, and directly with customers and founders on what gets built.

Everyone here works across the stack, but each engineer has a spike: the area where they set the bar for the team. You spend most of your time where yours is, and lean on your colleagues where theirs are.

  • Product: You build best in class products for the core jobs in freight forwarding, one job at a time. You work as a design partner with our customers to understand the work deeply, turn that understanding into a product they would choose over anything else, and feed what you learn back into the platform everyone builds on.

  • AI: You raise the ceiling on what our AI can do and the floor on how reliably it does it. That spans high volume tasks like classification and extraction and deep workflow tasks that run for hours. You design for performance, reliability, explainability and control, set up the gyms and evals to measure them, and build the harness that runs our agents in all of our products.

  • Platform: You own the foundation every product stands on: the runtime for thousands of concurrent agents and workflows, the way they communicate and scale, the controls for how they access data with permissions that hold, and the observability to see and measure all of it. You ensure the rest of the team can move fast without fear.

     

What we look for

  • A spike, with evidence. Something you have been exceptional at and proof of it. We hire on slope rather than years, so there is no experience threshold in either direction.

  • Strong fundamentals. In the AI-assisted era, having good technical judgement is key. You have shipped production systems people depend on, seen them fail and learned from it.

  • High agency and ownership. You take an ambiguous problem, make a call, and see it through.

  • Humility and learning velocity. You want to get better and you change your mind when the evidence says so.

  • Interest in the problem. You do not need a freight background, but you need to find messy real-world operations interesting rather than a chore.

     

Why join

You will shape the product, the architecture and the company, working alongside an engineering team from Palantir, Raft, Faculty, UnlikelyAI and Oxford. You will work directly with the businesses using what you build, on AI applied to an industry that has resisted software for decades. You will get meaningful equity, so when this works you share in it.

AI Fluency:
Norm prefers all team members to be fluent in AI. Successful candidates actively use AI in their day-to-day work to support thinking, creation, and problem-solving. They use it to improve the quality and speed of their work and to continuously refine how work gets done end-to-end.

Candidates should be prepared to demonstrate and discuss their AI usage throughout the interview process, including concrete examples of tools, workflows, and outcomes. We look for practical, hands-on experience, not theoretical familiarity.

This Role

As a Commercial Contracts Associate (NDA), you will work on a high impact team that provides important services to Norm Law’s clients, while using AI agents to streamline the drafting, review, and execution process in providing non-disclosure agreement review for clients. You’ll collaborate closely with partners, clients, and technology teams to deliver efficient, precise, and data-driven legal services for in-house legal teams of leading asset managers.

Our practice embraces the use of AI to reduce burden and increase your ability to focus on strategic legal judgment and client engagement.

What You'll Do

  • Document Drafting, Review, and Negotiation: Leverage AI agents to generate, compare, negotiate, and redline NDAs tailored to client guidelines

  • Client Advisory: Partner with clients to demonstrate how AI-assisted workflows improve accuracy, transparency, and velocity.

What We're Looking For

Core Qualifications

  • Qualified solicitor admitted in England and Wales, with a current Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) practising certificate.

  • 2-3+ years of experience reviewing NDAs or similar agreements.

  • Strong drafting and communication skills; meticulous attention to detail.

  • Interest in applying technology to enhance traditional deal workflows.

What Success Looks Like

  • 30 Days: Learn firm AI platforms; begin supporting the commercial contracts team using AI-enabled review and drafting.

  • 60 Days: Independently manage discrete components of NDA review with AI support.

  • 90 Days: Lead AI-augmented workstreams in live NDA reviews, improving efficiency and accuracy in document management and execution processes.

Benefits

Benefits: pension plan with an employer contribution, medical and dental insurance coverage, employee referral bonus program, initial 2 week onboarding in the US.

Work Location

Location: Central London

Work model: Hybrid

In-office expectation: 4-5 days per week

Why Join Norm Law

You’ll be part of the founding UK team bringing a proven US category leader to a receptive UK market. You’ll have autonomy, visibility, and the opportunity to build meaningful relationships — backed by a world-class product, an experienced executive team, and a growing global reputation.

To learn more about Norm, visit our website.

raw.description:
Who we are?

Silverfin is a cutting-edge cloud software solution built by accountants, for accountants. 

Founded in 2013, Silverfin was created to solve the frustrations of manual, error-prone processes in analysing financial data and compliance. From day one, we’ve been a cloud-first platform with an open API architecture, leveraging structured data to transform how accountants work.

Our mission is simple: to enhance and support the accountancy profession through AI and automation, ensuring accountants remain relevant and respected in the future of finance.

In 2023, Silverfin became part of the Visma Group, joining one of Europe’s leading providers of cloud software. This partnership strengthens our ability to innovate and expand our impact within the accountancy industry.

Today, Silverfin is trusted by over +1000 firms across 19 countries. Our clients include all of the Big 4 accounting firms, as well as leading global networks like BDO, PKF, Baker Tilly, Grant Thornton, and Moore.

Headquartered in Ghent, with offices in Mont-Saint-Guibert (BE), London (UK), Luxembourg (LU), and Gouda (NL), we’re a team of over 200 people - including a diverse remote engineering team working across multiple time zones - all working together to drive innovation in accounting.

How would you support our success?

Your role

We are on the lookout for a Senior Field Marketing Executive to join our team in the UKI. 

Your focus area will include a mix of marketing and event activities. You will be supporting events,  digital,  customer and partner marketing, and other field marketing activities in UKI, from our office in London. The position also includes occasional off-site event coordination mostly during office hours. 

That means organising events with project boards on Monday.com, messaging, creatives, stakeholders and budgets will be a very important responsibility in this role, next to regular marketing campaigns to our audience of accounting practices in the region.

As part of this journey, you'll be in sync with a fantastic team of 15 marketing team members across UKI, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg & Denmark. You’ll report to our Senior Manager Global Field Marketing, based at our head office in Ghent, Belgium. Your main focus region is the UKI. We provide a permanent contract on a full-time basis.

Silverfin moves fast with a constant flow of activities for both users and prospects, not to mention our incredible team. We also prioritise the well-being of our people, offering a range of initiatives. Envision yourself joining our international Marketing team and a diverse, motivated team, and growing along with Silverfin.

 

Your responsibilities

  • Collaborate with your BU stakeholders to define and refine the marketing plan for the UKI.

  • Work closely with the global marketing demand generation team based in Ghent. This team of specialists leads the execution of global targeted marketing campaigns aimed at generating leads and increasing demand utilising a variety of channels, including email, social media, PPC, and content marketing.

  • Work closely with the UKI sales team to ensure they have the marketing materials including assisting in the creation of sales enablement tools such as presentations, brochures, and case studies.

  • Plan, organise, and execute both hosted and 3rd party events from concept to completion. This includes venue selection, vendor management, promotional activities, and post-event analysis.

  • Measure and report on the effectiveness of marketing campaigns and events, using data to support decisions and improve future marketing strategies.

  • Liaise with product, sales, customer success and marketing teams to ensure cohesive brand messaging and optimise campaign success

  • Manage internal and external creative agencies to produce content such as video, copywriting, stand building etc.

  • Manage the marketing budget for the UKI  with expenses and allocation of budget spends

  • Focus on ABM methodology using our existing framework and infrastructure, which is supported by the whole marketing department; 

    • Improve account engagement in the UKI and account penetration in your target accounts for Tier 1 and 2 using a one-to-few approach. Expand the account-level ABM score with regional partners who provide engagement and buyer intent data. This complements the demand generation team, which runs a one-to-many digital strategy for Tier 3 and 4 accounts.

    • Report on ABM KPIs: account engagement, coverage across the buying committee, meetings booked, pipeline influenced and sourced, win rate and deal velocity

    • Showing ABM impact to senior leadership with clear, data-backed narratives

    • Testing, learning and improving programmes based on results

What will support your success?

Experience and Qualifications

  • Bachelor/Master in Marketing  

  • Proven marketing experience in B2B SaaS (5+ years)  

  • But even more important is your eagerness to deliver results and proactive attitude.

Attitude and personality-related traits

We’re looking for someone who can work autonomously, has a pragmatic approach, and is eager to deliver results. You’re also happy to travel occasionally to our head office in Ghent for training, workshops and meetings with your manager and most of the global marketing team.

Skills and knowledge

  • Essential:

    • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to write clear, persuasive copy for a UKI professional audience

    • Strong planning & prioritising skills. Organised (KANBAN), punctual (Deadlines), and meticulous (Quality). 

    • Salesforce: create campaigns, dashboards, and reports for your campaigns

    • Hubspot - follow up on emails, landing pages, segmentation

    • Tools like “Monday”, “Slack”, “Google Drive/Docs/Sheets”, “Canva”, “Eventbrite”, “Wordpress”

    • Event management of in-person events

  • Big Plus:

    • Comfortable running webinars/podcasts

    • Experience in devising & executing a marketing plan + budget

    • Experience with ABM programmatic and 1 to few

We care for you

Be part of something bigger - Join a growing SaaS company that’s now proudly part of Visma, Europe’s leader in mission-critical cloud software.

A connected team - Take part in regular team activities, retreats, and offsites to keep our culture thriving.

Grow with us - Take advantage of career development opportunities and a personal training allowance to support your growth.

UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable.

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

About the role

UFORCE is looking for a Chief Engineer, Air to lead the engineering of our Western-facing air platforms and turn operational lessons from Ukraine into reliable, manufacturable products that global customers can test, deploy and reorder.

You’ll own the technical baseline across the air portfolio, initially focusing on Platform N and expanding to other platforms sold outside Ukraine. You’ll work closely with Ukrainian engineering teams to understand the wider Nemesis pipeline, translate field experience into product improvements and build a consistent view of configurations and engineering evidence across the portfolio.

This is a hands-on senior technical leadership role. You’ll stay close to the hardware and the field, build a small engineering team, and bring engineering, manufacturing, supply chain and commercial partners together to deliver products at pace without compromising technical rigor.

The role is based in the UK and involves regular travel to engineering teams, manufacturing sites, test ranges and customers. Reporting arrangements and travel expectations will be confirmed during the hiring process.

What you’ll do

  • Own the air portfolio’s technical baseline. Establish controlled requirements, configurations, bills of materials and test evidence, starting with Platform N and extending across Western and Ukrainian air platforms. Put clear ownership and practical change control in place.

  • Lead end-to-end systems engineering. Make and coordinate technical decisions across airframe, propulsion, power, avionics, flight control, communications, navigation, payload interfaces, software interfaces and ground systems, bringing in specialists where needed.

  • Improve reliability and performance. Establish a disciplined failure-reporting and corrective-action process, investigate priority field and test issues, and demonstrate improvements against agreed requirements through repeatable testing.

  • Turn operational lessons into product improvements. Work with Ukrainian engineering and field teams to understand what has worked, capture operator feedback and agree a prioritised design-change roadmap for Western variants.

  • Build for repeatable production. Lead design-for-manufacture reviews and partner with manufacturing teams to release production-ready engineering packages for US and allied sites.

  • Strengthen the supply chain and cost position. Work with supply-chain and compliance partners to assess component sourcing, qualification, capacity and critical supplier risks. Develop a unit-cost roadmap and evaluate where components and systems should be built across UFORCE locations.

  • Support go-to-market and customer delivery. Partner with Sales and Business Development on customer requirements, priority markets, product positioning and business cases. Provide technical input on configurations, capability claims, pricing, delivery and support assumptions.

  • Prepare for trials and launch. Establish technical readiness gates covering demonstrations, compliance evidence, production readiness and handover to field support. Communicate product capabilities and limitations honestly to customers and test authorities.

  • Set the direction and build the team. Work with founders, Ukrainian colleagues and global leadership to develop the air product roadmap. Hire and develop engineers, establish clear ownership and build the practices needed as the function grows.

Required Skill

  • Experience leading the design and development of a complete UAS, with personal ownership of system-level technical decisions and demonstrated flight or field outcomes.

  • Strong systems engineering judgement across airframe, propulsion, power, avionics, flight control, communications, navigation and software interfaces.

  • Experience taking an aerial or comparable electromechanical product from prototype into repeatable production, including design for manufacture, configuration control and production testing.

  • A track record of investigating field failures, identifying root causes and measurably improving reliability through verified corrective actions.

  • Practical experience with applicable NDAA / Blue UAS sourcing requirements, restricted components and export-control considerations, including qualification or re-sourcing decisions.

  • Understanding of how contested operating conditions, including GNSS denial, jamming and communications resilience, influence product requirements and testing.

  • Experience supporting customer trials, competitions or tenders and communicating technical capabilities, limitations and risks to customers or test authorities.

  • Experience hiring or developing engineers and leading multidisciplinary teams across organisational and geographic boundaries.

  • Sound judgement on cost, performance, production readiness and supplier trade-offs, with the ability to make decisions in an evolving startup environment.

  • A hands-on approach, clear communication and the ability to balance speed with appropriate engineering discipline.

  • Willingness to travel regularly to engineering teams, manufacturing sites, test ranges and customers.

Nice to Have

  • Direct experience working with Ukrainian UAS teams, products or operators.

  • Experience with military or Ministry of Defence contracts.

  • Experience with military or civil airworthiness, qualification or certification.

  • Experience with payload integration or payload-release systems.

  • Experience coordinating engineering and manufacturing across multiple countries.

raw.description:
About the role

This is a permanent, part-time role, working two days a week. Unity is a scaling business with strong reward foundations already in place. We now need a senior reward specialist to strengthen them, fill the gaps and shape them into a framework that grows with the firm. We want reward that reflects how Unity actually works: Partner-led client teams, Functional Leader-led enablement teams, and a culture built on trust, direct feedback and progress over process. We don’t want a generic framework lifted from a larger, more traditional firm.

You’ll take what we have, judge what’s working and what isn’t, and build it out where it needs to go next. You’ll also run it: pay reviews, benefits renewals, and the data and reporting that keep it trusted. You’ll refine it each cycle and make sure the framework is well documented and easy for others to work with.

It suits someone who gets energy from building and improving, and who knows that reward only proves itself once it’s live. You’ll be comfortable with ambiguity and confident making judgement calls. You’ll respect what’s already been done while being willing to challenge it. You’ll also take satisfaction in the steady work of keeping a system accurate, fair and well-run.

This is a role where one expert can own reward end to end, without needing a full-time seat. It will suit an experienced reward specialist who wants a senior, high-impact role with a bounded commitment, including people with a fractional or portfolio background who now want a permanent home.


What you’ll own

  • Reward strategy and philosophy: build on and evolve Unity’s approach to pay. That covers how we position against the market, how pay works across client-facing and enablement tracks, and how reward reinforces Unity’s “progress over process” culture rather than working against it.

  • Pay structure and benchmarking: develop and maintain salary bands and grading across roles and levels, benchmarked against relevant professional services and advisory market data.

  • Pay review cycles: design and run the annual (or biannual) pay and bonus review. That includes timelines, guidance for Partners and Functional Leaders, calibration support, and sign-off with the Management Team / Partners Group.

  • Benefits: own the benefits offering end to end, including provider relationships, renewals, flexible benefits design and clear communication of value to employees.

  • Pay equity and compliance: run regular pay equity analysis (including gender pay gap reporting where applicable), keep Unity compliant with UK reward-related employment law, and flag risk to the CPO early.

  • Reward governance and data: keep reward data accurate and current in our people systems, and produce clear reporting for the Management Team on pay spend, equity and market position.

  • Advisory support: partner directly with Partners and Functional Leaders on individual pay decisions, such as new hire offers, promotions and retention cases. Your recommendations will be clear, defensible and grounded in the framework, not one-off improvisation.

  • The future of reward at Unity: work with the CPO to shape how reward evolves as the firm grows, including the capability, capacity and structure we’ll need over time.


What success looks like in your first 12 months

  • A refined, published pay and grading framework that Partners and Functional Leaders trust and actually use

  • A clean, well-governed annual pay review with no surprises for the Management Team

  • Reward decisions that are consistent, benchmarked and easy to explain, in keeping with Unity’s “trust and accountability” and “no surprises” principles

  • Reward documented and embedded, so that the framework is understood, easy to work with and keeps improving with each cycle


What we’re looking for

  • Senior reward / compensation and benefits experience, ideally including time in professional services, consulting or another partnership-style environment

  • Equally at home developing and extending an existing framework and running it well day to day, from benchmarking data and banding mechanics to benefits contracts and review timelines

  • Someone who sees the operational side of reward as part of the craft. Each pay cycle, renewal and equity report is a chance to test and improve the framework.

  • A pragmatic operator who can deliver across the full scope of reward in two focused days a week, prioritising the highest-leverage work first

  • Confident advising Partners and senior leaders directly, with recommendations grounded in evidence rather than precedent alone

  • Comfortable working with light process and high trust, building just enough structure and no more

  • Experience of part-time, interim or fractional working is welcome, but not required. We value people who can make an impact quickly and build things that last.


How this role fits at Unity

You’ll sit in the People Team, working closely with the Chief People Officer, the Performance Lead (a fellow part-time specialist), People Ops, and Partners and Functional Leaders across the business. Reward decisions at Unity draw on the same “collective insight, direct feedback” approach that runs through how the firm manages performance and probation. They’re calibrated and evidence-based, never made in isolation.
